globals.spl_root: the folder of the study on the SAS server (the one line a program sets: %LET spl_root = ...;)
globals.spl_program: the name of the program, set by %study
globals.spl_quiet: yes: no begin and end lines of the macros in the log (%LET spl_quiet = yes; before the calls)

macros.name: _spl_arg
macros.purpose: One parameter of a call that a one-call table writes into its long program: its name and its value. A parameter without a value is left out.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements that add the parameter to the arrays PN and PV of %_spl_program(begin).
macros.des: One parameter of a call in the long program of a one-call table (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: _name
parameters.description: The name of the parameter in the call; without _value also the parameter of the calling macro whose value is written

parameters.name: _value
parameters.description: A DATA step expression with the value (a text)

macros.example:
%_spl_arg(data, "&rec.")
%_spl_arg(where)

macros.name: _spl_begin
macros.purpose: The begin line of a macro in the log, with the version of the macro library; it gives the time it began, for the end line (%_spl_end). The version below is the one place of the version of the library: every header says the same.
macros.output: TEXT: the text of the time it began (seconds); the line NOTE: [describe] begins (Sapling macro library 1.1.0). in the log, unless SPL_QUIET is yes (a global macro variable: %LET spl_quiet = yes; before the calls keeps the log short).
macros.des: The begin line of a macro in the log

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

macros.example: %LET t0 = %_spl_begin(describe);

macros.name: _spl_call
macros.purpose: One call of a macro in the long program of a one-call table: the parameters given by %_spl_arg since the last call, one per line, the equal signs under each other.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements that write the call to the file of the long program and start the next list of parameters.
macros.des: One call of a macro in the long program of a one-call table (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the macro called, without the percent sign

macros.example: %_spl_call(freq)

macros.name: _spl_chars
macros.purpose: The character variables among some variables of a data set (their names, separated by blanks). The statistics macros give them one length ($200) in their results, so that results stack without a cut value.
macros.output: TEXT: the names of the character variables among VARS, separated by blanks (a variable not in DATA is left out).
macros.des: The character variables among some variables of a data set

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set (data set options after it are ignored)

parameters.name: vars
parameters.description: The variables

macros.example: %LET chars = %_spl_chars(adae, TRT01A AEBODSYS AEDECOD AVISITN);

macros.name: _spl_csv
macros.purpose: Write a data set as a CSV file: a line with the names of the variables, then one line per row (a DATA step; values with a comma or a quote are quoted).
macros.output: FILE:  a line with the names of the variables, then one line per row.
macros.des: Write a data set as a CSV file (DATA steps)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set (data set options such as KEEP= are allowed)

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The CSV file to write

macros.example: %_spl_csv(data=l14_3_1(KEEP=usubjid aedecod), file=&spl_out./listings/l14_3_1.csv)

macros.name: _spl_empty
macros.purpose: The result of a statistics macro when no record qualifies: the result shape without a row, and a NOTE that says so. A procedure never runs on no record, so the log has no error of one.
macros.output: OUT: KEEP, ADD, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT and no row; the line NOTE: [macro] No data qualified ... in the log.
macros.des: The result shape without a row: no data qualified

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: The group variables of the result (BY, WITHIN)

parameters.name: macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: like
parameters.description: The records (without a row): the types and lengths of the group variables

parameters.name: add
parameters.description: Character group variables the records do not have (VERSUS)

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The result to write

macros.example: %_spl_empty(macro=cox, out=&out., like=_cox_records, keep=&by. &within., add=versus)

macros.name: _spl_end
macros.purpose: The end line of a macro in the log: its run time since its begin line (%_spl_begin), and with debug=yes that its work data sets are kept.
macros.output: LOG: NOTE: [describe] ends after 0.42 seconds. in the log, unless SPL_QUIET is yes; with debug=yes always the line that names the kept work data sets.
macros.des: The end line of a macro in the log

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: _start
parameters.description: The time it began (%_spl_begin)

parameters.name: _debug
parameters.description: The debug= of the calling macro

macros.example: %_spl_end(describe, &t0., &debug.)

macros.name: _spl_figure_attrs
macros.purpose: The look of the groups of a figure: an attribute map (DATTRMAP=) that gives each value of the group variable a colour, a marker and a line pattern, in the order of the columns of %columns (columns=; a value not in it after them), else in the order the values come in the data. Eight colours safe for colour blindness (Okabe and Ito, without the yellow, and a grey), each with another marker and line pattern, so that groups differ in black and white too; a ninth group starts the list again. ID grp has all attributes; ID grpcol the colours only, solid lines (an error bar; a marker of its own, such as the censoring mark: give it to a copy of the group variable, as SGPLOT takes one ID per variable). The data get _ORDER, the place of their group.
macros.output: OUT: the attribute map: ID, VALUE, _ORDER and the attributes; DATA: data= with _ORDER.
macros.des: The colours, markers and line patterns of the groups of a figure

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The rows of the figure: they get _ORDER

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: The columns of %columns (COL, COLVALUE)

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The group variable

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The attribute map

macros.example: %_spl_figure_attrs(data=_kmplot_plot, columns=&columns., var=&by., out=_kmplot_attrs)

macros.name: _spl_figure_close
macros.purpose: Close the destinations of a figure (%_spl_figure_open) and set back what it changed: the RTF file closed, LISTING closed and opened again (its style LISTING) when it was open before, the options of ODS GRAPHICS reset.
macros.output: CODE: the ODS statements that close the destinations.
macros.des: Close the destinations of a figure and set back what it changed

parameters.name: listing
parameters.description: yes: LISTING was open before the figure

macros.example: %_spl_figure_close(listing=&listing.)

macros.name: _spl_figure_dodge
macros.purpose: Move the groups a little apart on a numeric x axis, so that their error bars do not overlap: _XPLOT = x + (_ORDER - (G + 1) / 2) * STEP, G the number of groups, STEP the smaller of half the smallest distance of two x values divided by G - 1 and 3% of the range of x. The x of the data stays as it is. With offset= the room the axis needs at each end, so that the outer groups are not cut at the edge of the plot.
macros.output: DATA: data= with _XPLOT; with offset= that macro variable.
macros.des: Move the groups of a figure a little apart on the x axis

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The rows of the figure, with _ORDER (%_spl_figure_attrs)

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The numeric x variable

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: A macro variable of the caller: it gets the offset of each end of the axis (OFFSETMIN=, OFFSETMAX= of COLAXIS), a fraction of its length

macros.example: %_spl_figure_dodge(data=_meanplot_plot, x=x, offset=xoff)

macros.name: _spl_figure_label
macros.purpose: The label of an axis, as a text in quotes: the text given (in quotes, or put in quotes), else the label of the variable, else its name.
macros.output: TEXT: the label in double quotes.
macros.des: The label of an axis, in quotes

parameters.name: _data
parameters.description: The data set

parameters.name: _var
parameters.description: The variable of the axis

parameters.name: _text
parameters.description: The text given, or nothing

macros.example: %LET xlabel = %_spl_figure_label(&data., &time., %SUPERQ(xlabel));

macros.name: _spl_figure_nodata
macros.purpose: No record qualified for a figure: out= in the shape of the figure with no row, the NOTE No data qualified, and the figure that says so (a blank plot with the text, in the PNG and the RTF of file=, under the titles of the program).
macros.output: OUT: no row; FILE: <file>.png and <file>.rtf with the text.
macros.des: The figure and the result when no record qualified

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: The variables of like= kept in out=

parameters.name: macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: like
parameters.description: The records, without a row

parameters.name: chars
parameters.description: Character variables of out= ($200)

parameters.name: nums
parameters.description: Numeric variables of out=

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The output without its extension

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The width of the figure

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The height of the figure

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The result to write (none: no data set)

macros.example:
%_spl_figure_nodata(
     keep   = &by.
   , macro  = kmplot
   , like   = _kmplot_records
   , chars  = kind
   , nums   = x y n censored
   , file   = &file.
   , width  = &width.
   , height = &height.
   , out    = &out.
 )

macros.name: _spl_figure_open
macros.purpose: Open the destinations of one figure: the PNG image (the LISTING destination with GPATH=, 300 dpi, image name and size from ODS GRAPHICS) and the RTF file with the figure on a page (the titles and footnotes of the program as text of the page: NOGTITLE NOGFOOTNOTE). The PNG carries the titles and the footnotes in the image (LISTING draws them in the graph, as SAS does by default), so a PNG alone says what it is. Both use the style HTMLBLUE: tick values 9pt, axis labels and legend 10pt, titles 11pt. It notes in the macro variable named by state= whether LISTING was open, for %_spl_figure_close.
macros.output: CODE: the ODS statements that open the destinations.
macros.des: Open the PNG and RTF destinations of a figure

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The output without its extension: <file>.png and <file>.rtf

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The width of the figure

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The height of the figure

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The name of a local macro variable of the caller: yes when LISTING was open, else no

macros.example: %_spl_figure_open(file=&file., width=&width., height=&height., state=LISTING)

macros.name: _spl_figure_outpar
macros.purpose: The drawing parameters of a figure macro as a data set (its outpar=): one row per parameter in the order of the signature, PARAMETER its name in lower case and VALUE its value as the macro draws it (given, from par=, the default, or made by the macro: the label of an axis, the format of the ticks). par= of a later call reads it back.
macros.output: DATA: out= with PARAMETER ($32) and VALUE ($500).
macros.des: Write the drawing parameters of a figure macro as a data set

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: The drawing parameters of the caller, in their order (names= of %_spl_figure_par)

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The data set to write; blank: none

macros.example: %_spl_figure_outpar(names=&drawn., out=&outpar.)

macros.name: _spl_figure_par
macros.purpose: The parameters of a figure macro, before its checks. With plot= (draw the out= of a call again): data= is not given, plot= has the variables of out=, and each parameter of the computation that has a value gets a NOTE (it is not used). With par= (the outpar= of a call): each drawing parameter that the call leaves blank gets the VALUE of its row; a row that names no drawing parameter is an error. Then each parameter still blank gets its default from draw= or compute=. So a value in the call wins over a row of par=, and a row of par= over the default: the defaults of these parameters are here, not in the signature of the macro.
macros.output: LOG: one ERROR with its fix for a wrong plot= or par=, a NOTE for each parameter not used. The local macro variables of the caller: the parameters set from par= and from the defaults, state= and names=.
macros.des: Read par= and the defaults of a figure macro, and check plot=

parameters.name: macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: draw
parameters.description: Its drawing parameters in the order of its signature, each as name or name=default

parameters.name: compute
parameters.description: Its parameters of the computation that plot= does not use, each as name or name=default

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: The variables of its out= that plot= must have

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: The name of a local macro variable of the caller: the names of the drawing parameters

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The name of a local macro variable of the caller: 1 when the parameters are right, else 0

macros.example:
%_spl_figure_par(
     macro   = kmplot
   , draw    = columns by panel atrisk=yes xlabel ylabel="Survival (%)" file
   , compute = where time cnsr=CNSR
   , shape   = kind x y lower upper n censored
   , names   = drawn
   , state   = ok
 )

macros.name: _spl_folder
macros.purpose: Make the folder of a file the macro writes, and each folder above it that is missing, with a NOTE that names the folder made. A path that starts with ~ is in the home folder. Nothing is made when the folder is there or the file has no folder.
macros.output: LOG: NOTE: [print] made the folder ~/study/out/tlf. for a folder it made; a WARNING when the folder cannot be made.
macros.des: Make the folder of a file and the folders above it that are missing

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro

parameters.name: _file
parameters.description: The file the macro writes: a path

macros.example: %_spl_folder(print, %SUPERQ(file).rtf)

macros.name: _spl_levels
macros.purpose: The planned categories of some variables as rows: every combination of their values, by DO loops. A character variable gets the length $200.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements: LENGTH of the character variables ($200), then DO loops that output every combination of the planned values (DO BNRIND = ...; DO ANRIND = ...; OUTPUT; END; END;); with order= also the place of each value in its list.
macros.des: The planned categories of some variables as rows (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set of the variables (it tells which ones are character)

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Each variable followed by its values: a text in quotes, a number without

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: A prefix: the place of each value in its list as the variables <prefix>1, <prefix>2 ... (one for each variable, in the order of levels=)

macros.name: _spl_need
macros.purpose: Check the parameters a macro needs: each must have a value, and a data set of data=, denom=, columns= or from= must exist. For each one that does not it writes one line that names the parameter and the fix: ERROR: [describe] data= is required: give data=<value> ... ERROR: [describe] data=adsx does not exist: give data= ... It gives 1 when all are there, 0 when one is not: the caller then stops (%RETURN).
macros.output: TEXT: 1 or 0, as text.
macros.des: Check the parameters a macro needs

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro (for the message)

parameters.name: _params
parameters.description: The names of its parameters that must have a value

macros.example: %IF not %_spl_need(describe, data var by out) %THEN %RETURN;

macros.name: _spl_nobs
macros.purpose: The number of rows of a data set (with the WHERE= of its data set options, when it has one); 0 when the data set does not exist.
macros.output: TEXT: the number, as text.
macros.des: The number of rows of a data set

parameters.name: _data
parameters.description: The data set

macros.example: %IF %_spl_nobs(_describe_values) = 0 %THEN %DO;

macros.name: _spl_oneof
macros.purpose: Check that the value of a parameter is one of a list (in any case). When it is not it writes one line that names the parameter and the fix: ERROR: [cox] ties=fast is not one of efron breslow exact ... It gives 1 or 0: the caller then stops (%RETURN).
macros.output: TEXT: 1 or 0, as text.
macros.des: Check that a parameter is one of a list

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro (for the message)

parameters.name: _param
parameters.description: The parameter

parameters.name: _list
parameters.description: Its values, separated by blanks

macros.example: %IF not %_spl_oneof(cox, ties, efron breslow exact discrete) %THEN %RETURN;

macros.name: _spl_pairlist
macros.purpose: The pairs of groups of a parameter as rows: _K (the place of the pair), _A (the group) and _B (the group it is compared with). The pairs are separated by #, one pair per line, the first group against the second; a value with a blank or a hyphen is in quotes: pairs = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo" # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo" The form of version 1.0 is still read: "A"-"B" "C"-"D" (no #, every item a pair joined by a hyphen outside quotes).
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements: one row (OUTPUT) per pair with _K, _A and _B ($200).
macros.des: The pairs of groups of a parameter as rows _K _A _B (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: The parameter of the calling macro that holds the pairs (pairs, family)

macros.name: _spl_pairs
macros.purpose: The differences of the pairs of groups asked for, from the table Diffs of PROC MIXED (it has each pair once, in one direction). It computes nothing: a difference the other way round is the same difference with its sign and its limits turned.
macros.output: OUT: WITHIN, BY (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl, pval: one row per pair asked for (in each group of WITHIN).
macros.des: The differences of the pairs of groups asked for, from the table Diffs of a procedure

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: a character variable

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: The variables of the separate models (BY groups of PROC MIXED)

parameters.name: diffs
parameters.description: The Diffs table (the group in BY, the group it is compared with in _BY)

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: The records of the model (for the groups and their order)

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of ORDER (else of the values); or the pairs separated by #, the group first, then the group it is compared with (%_spl_pairlist reads them, and the form "A"-"B" of 1.0)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: A numeric variable of the records with one value per group

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The data set: WITHIN, BY (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl, pval

macros.example:
%_spl_pairs(
     by      = trt01p
   , within  =
   , diffs   = _lsmeans_diffs
   , records = _lsmeans_records
   , pairs   = all
   , order   = trt01pn
   , out     = _lsmeans_pairs
 )

macros.name: _spl_program
macros.purpose: The fixed parts of the DATA step with which a one-call table writes its long program: begin (the file and the variables), records (the population and the records, from the parameters ADSL, POP, DATA, WHERE and NAME of the calling macro), table (the %table call, from BY, ORDER, TOTAL, FORMAT, FILE, NAME and DEBUG, with the TITLE and FOOTNOTE statements of TITLE and FOOTNOTE before it and their clearing after it), titles and untitled (those statements alone), end (the routine that writes a call). It computes nothing.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements. It reads the macro variables REC (the records the calls read), POPN (the data set with the N of the columns), DS and NAMES of the calling macro.
macros.des: The fixed parts of the long program of a one-call table (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: _part
parameters.description: begin, names, label, records, table, titles, untitled or end

parameters.name: _var
parameters.description: With label: the variable of the block, in lower case

macros.example:
DATA _NULL_;
  %_spl_program(begin)
  %_spl_program(records)
  %_spl_arg(data, "&rec.")
  %_spl_call(freq)
  %_spl_program(table)
  %_spl_program(end)
RUN;

macros.name: _spl_quote
macros.purpose: The value of a parameter as a text in single quotes, for a DATA step: each single quote in it doubled, nothing in it resolved. The code the macro writes holds the value itself (SYMGET would read it when the step runs), so that the flat program (the code the macros wrote, without a macro) has it too. An empty value gives a blank text.
macros.output: TEXT: a text in single quotes: 'Age (years)', '"A" "B" # "C" "B"'.
macros.des: The value of a parameter as a text in single quotes (DATA step code)

parameters.name: _param
parameters.description: The name of the parameter (label, pairs)

macros.example: block = DEQUOTE(%_spl_quote(label));

macros.name: _spl_rows
macros.purpose: The result shape: one row per statistic of the row just read. Each statistic is a numeric variable of the same name (n, mean, pval ...); the row gets STAT (its name), VALUE (its number), PATTERN and TEXT (the number as printed, %_spl_text: a p value, pval or padj, never as 0 or 1).
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements: one row per statistic with STAT, VALUE and TEXT. The default patterns: XX for n, events, min, max; XX.X for mean, median, q1, q3, lsmean, diff, estimate, lcl, ucl; (XX.X%) for pct; X.XXX for pval; XX.XX for sd, se, lsmean_se, diff_se and any other statistic.
macros.des: The result shape: one row per statistic (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: missing
parameters.description: The text of a statistic without a value (default blank; %km gives NE: not estimable)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics in their order, each with its pattern (mean="XX.X") or without (the default pattern of the statistic below)

macros.name: _spl_stackpairs
macros.purpose: The records of each pair of groups asked for, one under the other: the pair (_PAIR), its group (_A) and the group it is compared with (_B), and the side of each record (_SIDE: 1 in _A, 2 in _B). A procedure then runs BY _PAIR _A _B on the 2 groups of each pair, the group first. It computes nothing.
macros.output: OUT: the records of each pair with _PAIR, _A, _B and _SIDE (1 in _A, 2 in _B), sorted by them. The macro variable PAIRSOK of the caller: 1, or 0 when a pair names a group that no record has (an error in the log).
macros.des: The records of each pair of groups asked for, one under the other

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: a character variable

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: The records (one per subject)

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of ORDER (else of the values); or the pairs separated by #, the group first, then the group it is compared with (%_spl_pairlist reads them, and the form "A"-"B" of 1.0)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: A numeric variable of the records with one value per group

parameters.name: macro
parameters.description: The macro that calls (for the message)

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The data set: the records of each pair with _PAIR, _A, _B, _SIDE, sorted by them

macros.example:
%_spl_stackpairs(
     macro   = ttest
   , records = _ttest_records
   , by      = trt01p
   , pairs   = all
   , order   = trt01pn
   , out     = _ttest_pairs
 )

macros.name: _spl_text
macros.purpose: The text of a number by its pattern. A pattern shows one number as one group of X: XX, XX.X, (XX.X%), (N=XX). The number is rounded (ROUND) to the decimals of the X group, right aligned in its width and put in its place; the text is trimmed. A p value never prints as 0 or 1: rounded to 0 it is < and the smallest step (X.XXX: <0.001), rounded to 1 it is > and one step less (>0.999). The number is unchanged.
macros.output: CODE: DATA step statements: TEXT is the number of VALUE as its PATTERN shows it (9.46 with (XX.X%) gives ( 9.5%); 86 with (N=XX) gives (N=86); 3 with XX gives 3; a p value 0.00004 with X.XXX gives <0.001).
macros.des: The text of a number by its pattern (DATA step statements)

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The numeric variable

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The character variable with the pattern

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: The character variable to write (blank when the number is missing)

parameters.name: pvalue
parameters.description: A condition that is true when the number is a p value (STAT IN ('pval' 'padj'))

macros.name: _spl_total
macros.purpose: The name of the group of all groups together, from total=: nothing for no, Total for yes, else the text in quotes.
macros.output: TEXT: nothing for no (or empty), Total for yes, else the text of the quotes.
macros.des: The name of the group of all groups together, from total=

parameters.name: total
parameters.description: The value of total= (no, yes, or a name in quotes)

macros.example: %LET totlab = %_spl_total(%SUPERQ(total));

macros.name: _spl_vars
macros.purpose: Check that the variables of some parameters are variables of a data set. For each one that is not it writes one line that names the parameter and the fix: ERROR: [describe] var=AGEX is not a variable of adsl: give ... It gives 1 when all are there, 0 when one is not: the caller then stops (%RETURN). A data set that cannot be opened is the business of %_spl_need. With _also (the subjects adsl= of a one-call table, whose variables go to the records) a variable of either data set is there.
macros.output: TEXT: 1 or 0, as text.
macros.des: Check that variables are in a data set

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The name of the calling macro (for the message)

parameters.name: _data
parameters.description: The parameter that names the data set (data, denom)

parameters.name: _params
parameters.description: The parameters whose values are variables of it

parameters.name: _also
parameters.description: The parameter that names a second data set where the variables may be (adsl)

macros.example:
%IF not %_spl_vars(describe, data, var by) %THEN %RETURN;
%IF not %_spl_vars(table_ae, data, var by, adsl) %THEN %RETURN;

macros.name: _spl_windows
macros.purpose: The rows of windows= (or visits=) of a call as a data set: one row per window, the rows of the call separated by #, the values of a row by blanks, a text in quotes, a missing number as a period.
macros.output: DATA: _out, one row per window in the order of the call. The macro variable ROWSOK of the caller: 1, or 0 when a row has not its number of values (an error in the log).
macros.des: The rows of windows= or visits= of a call as a data set

parameters.name: _macro
parameters.description: The macro that calls

parameters.name: _name
parameters.description: The name of its parameter with the rows

parameters.name: _kind

macros.name: adjust
macros.purpose:
Adds the adjusted p-values of a family of pairs of groups to a result: one row padj per pair. Use it after %lsmeans, %mmrm, %cox, %logistic, %risk, %rateratio, %ttest or %wilcoxon: it reads their rows with STAT pval. The family is the hypotheses of one multiplicity block: the pairs of family=, in their order. method= gives the adjustment:
- bonferroni: Bonferroni (PROC MULTTEST); with weights=, the weighted Bonferroni test in a DATA step (the p-value divided by its weight, at most 1)
- holm: Holm, the step-down Bonferroni test (PROC MULTTEST STEPBON)
- hochberg: Hochberg (PROC MULTTEST)
- hierarchy: the fixed sequence in a DATA step; each adjusted p-value is the largest p-value of its hypothesis and of the hypotheses before it
Every row of data= with STAT pval and a pair of family= is one hypothesis of the family. When data= has a pair in several rows (the terms, visits or subgroups of within=), all of them are adjusted together, as one family. For a family in each term, call %adjust once per term, on a data set with only the rows of that term (a DATA step with WHERE first).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answers: the risk differences of a family of pairs and their adjusted p-values (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the rows of data=, then one row per pair of the family with STAT padj, VALUE the adjusted p-value and TEXT the printed value. When data= has no p-value of a pair of family=, out= is data= as it is and the log has a NOTE.
macros.des: The adjusted p-values of a family of pairs of groups (PROC MULTTEST)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: A result of pairs with the variables of by=, VERSUS, STAT and VALUE: the out= of %lsmeans, %mmrm, %cox and the other macros of pairs

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: the variable of data= with the group of each pair (by = trt01p)

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: The pairs of the family in their order, separated by #: each the group first and then the group it is compared with, each value in quotes: family = "High" "Placebo" # "Low" "Placebo". A pair is in the direction of the rows of data= (the group in by=, then VERSUS): "Placebo" "High" does not find the row of High against Placebo.

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: The adjustment: bonferroni, holm, hochberg or hierarchy

parameters.name: weights
parameters.description: The weights of a weighted Bonferroni test: one number per pair, in the order of family=, separated by blanks (weights = 0.8 0.2). Only with method=bonferroni.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The pattern of the printed adjusted p-value, in quotes

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _adjust_*

macros.example:
* Adjusts the p values of the two comparisons against Placebo by Hochberg: PADJ after PVAL.;
%adjust(
     data   = sbp_ls
   , by     = trt01p
   , family = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , method = hochberg
   , out    = sbp_adj
 )

macros.name: aeplot
macros.purpose: Draws the percent and risk difference of each adverse event as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. Use %barplot for the percents of the categories of one variable without a difference. The figure has two panels side by side that share the axis of the terms. The left panel shows the percent of the subjects of each group with the term, as dots. The right panel shows the risk difference of each group against the reference group, with its confidence interval and a line at 0. The flags are those of %termflags and the risk differences those of %risk (ci=, level=), so the figure and a table made with them cannot differ. The terms are those that reach threshold=, in the order of sort=, at most max= of them. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.
macros.procedure: PROC SUMMARY, PROC SGPANEL (and PROC FREQ in %risk)
macros.proven: Its known answer: the percents and the Wald intervals, worked out by hand; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-27 (the cases of the 9 figure macros: 103 of 103 the same)
macros.output: OUT: the variable of term=, the variable of by=, KIND, X, LOWER, UPPER and N. A row of KIND percent is one term and group: X is the percent of its subjects and N the subjects with the term. A row of KIND difference is one term and group that is not the reference: X is the risk difference in percent (100 x RD of %risk), and LOWER and UPPER its limits in percent. OUTPAR: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). FILE: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.
macros.des: Adverse events: percent by group and risk difference (PROC SUMMARY, PROC SGPANEL)
macros.note: Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %aeplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed: the terms from the top in the order of their first row (to drop or move a term, change its rows). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, term, by, xlabel, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute (sort= and max= choose the rows of out= and their order); with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of denom=.

parameters.name: denom

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y')

parameters.name: term
parameters.description: The term of a row: one variable of data= (term = aebodsys)

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one character variable of denom=

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The reference group of the risk difference: a value of by=, in quotes (reference = 'Placebo')

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: A percent: only the terms that this percent of the subjects of a group or more have, in at least one group (threshold = 5)

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The order of the terms from the top: difference (the risk difference of the first group that is not the reference, the largest first), frequency (the percent of all subjects, the largest first) or alphabetical

parameters.name: ci

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1

   , out       = f_ae_risk

macros.name: ancova
macros.purpose: Returns the Type III p-value of one numeric term in a linear model, such as the test of a dose response (test = trt01pn): the test of one numeric term, not a comparison of the groups. For the ANCOVA comparison of the groups, use %lsmeans; for a model of repeated visits, %mmrm. The model is PROC GLM: the class factors, the covariates and the tested term, one record per subject (the first with a value; when where= leaves a second record of a subject, the log has a NOTE with their number). Give a where= that leaves one record per subject, such as one parameter at one visit with anl01fl = 'Y'; otherwise each subject has the first of its records in the order of data=, whichever it is. The coefficient of the term, its standard error and its confidence limits come when stats= asks for them. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack): one row per statistic, of all subjects together (GROUPS is blank). STAT is pval, estimate, se, lcl or ucl.
macros.des: The Type III test of a term in a linear model (PROC GLM)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set, with USUBJID

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The response: one numeric variable

parameters.name: covars
parameters.description: The covariates: numeric variables separated by blanks (covars = base)

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: The class factors: variables separated by blanks (class = sex)

parameters.name: test
parameters.description: The tested term: one numeric variable, such as a dose or the number of a treatment (test = trt01pn)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are pval, estimate, se, lcl and ucl. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _ancova_*

macros.example:
* Tests a linear dose response of the change at Week 12, adjusted for baseline: one p value.;
%ancova(
     data   = advs
   , where  = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12' AND anl01fl = 'Y')
   , var    = chg
   , covars = base
   , test   = trt01pn
   , label  = "Dose response"
   , out    = sbp_dose
 )

macros.name: anova
macros.purpose: Returns the p-value of the F test of a one-way analysis of variance of a variable between the groups. Use %ttest or %wilcoxon to compare pairs of groups, and %ancova when the model has covariates. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The model is var= by by= (PROC GLM). The p-value is that of the model, one test of all the groups together. A record with a missing value or a missing group is not used.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row: STAT pval, with GROUPS blank (all the groups together), BLOCK, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies, the result has no row.
macros.des: The F test of a one-way analysis of variance (PROC GLM)

macros.name: ard
macros.purpose:
Writes every number of a table to a CSV file, the numbers file. Use %csv for the records of a listing or the numbers of a figure. The numbers file has one line per number: the result it comes from, its statistic, the values of its groups, and the number as stored and as printed. The number as stored is the value written with the format BEST32.: at most 15 significant digits and at most 14 decimals, the digits after them cut, not rounded (664/9 is 73.7777777777777); the number as printed is the TEXT of the result. It reads the results, never the printed page, so that a second program, in SAS or R, can compare its numbers with this file.
- With columns=, the first lines are the N of each column (the result N).
- A number has the values of at most five groups (g1_value to g5_value), in the order of GROUPS.
macros.proven: The tables of a made-up study: 759 of 759 numbers the same as those of a second program in R; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: FILE: <out>/ard/<file>.csv, where <out> is the output folder that %study set and <file> is in lower case. Its columns: result (the name of the result), stat (the statistic), g1_value to g5_value (the values of the group variables in the order of GROUPS of the result: the column first, then the levels of the row, such as VERSUS of a comparison), raw (the value written with BEST32.: at most 15 significant digits and at most 14 decimals, the last digit cut, not rounded, so that 664/9 is 73.7777777777777; a whole number in full; blank for a missing value) and formatted (the printed text).
macros.des: Every number of a table as a CSV file, with every digit (DATA steps)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The stacked results (out= of %stack)

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: The columns (out= of %columns). When given, the N of each column comes first, as the result N.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The name of the numbers file, without its extension. When not given, it is the name of the program that %study set; without %study, file= is required.

* Writes every number of the table and each column N to one CSV file: the raw value and the text.;
%ard(data=t14_2_1, columns=t14_2_1_cols, file=t14_2_1)

macros.name: barplot
macros.purpose: Draws bars of the percent of each category by group as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. Use %aeplot for adverse events with their risk differences. With denom=, a bar is the percent of the subjects of the group in the population, and a subject counts once in a category; without it, the percent of the records of the group. stat=count gives the count instead of the percent. The groups stand side by side, or stacked in one bar with stacked=yes; the value is written on each bar. A record with a missing category, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.
macros.proven: Its known answer: the counts and the percents, worked out by hand; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-27 (the cases of the 9 figure macros: 103 of 103 the same)

These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

macros.name: chisq
macros.purpose: Returns the p-value of the Pearson chi-square test of the groups against the categories of a response. Use %fisher for subjects with a record against subjects without (an adverse event), and %cmh for a test within strata. The test has no continuity correction. Each subject counts once in each group and category. A record with a missing group, category or value of within= is not used. With exact=yes the macro gives Fisher's exact test of the same table. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answers: the chi-square test and the exact test (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack): one row with STAT pval, or one row per group of within= with the variables of within=. GROUPS has the names of the within= variables. VALUE is missing where PROC FREQ makes no test (a table with one row or one column).
macros.des: The Pearson chi-square test of groups against categories (PROC FREQ)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records, with USUBJID

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The categories of the response: one variable, numeric or character

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups to compare: one variable

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: One test in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as a parameter and a visit (within = paramcd avisit)

parameters.name: exact
parameters.description: yes: Fisher's exact test of the same table instead of the chi-square test

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistic pval and the pattern of its printed number, such as stats = pval="X.XXXX"

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _chisq_*

macros.example:
* Tests sex across the groups: one row, the p value of the chi square test.;
%chisq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_chisq
 )
* Runs the exact test of the normal range within each parameter: one p value per parameter.;
%chisq(
     data   = adlb
   , where  = (avisit = 'Week 24')
   , var    = anrind
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = paramcd
   , exact  = yes
   , out    = nr_test
 )

macros.name: cmh
macros.purpose:
Returns the p-value of the Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test of the groups against the categories of a response, within strata. Use %chisq for the same test without strata. Each subject counts once in each group, category and stratum. A record with a missing group, category or value of within= is not used. statistic= chooses the test:
- general: the test of general association
- rowmean: the test that the mean scores of the groups differ; the scores are the values of the numeric response (SCORES=TABLE)
The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack): one row with STAT pval, or one row per group of within= with the variables of within=. GROUPS has the names of the within= variables. VALUE is missing where PROC FREQ makes no test.
macros.des: The Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test of groups against categories in strata (PROC FREQ)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records, with USUBJID

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The categories of the response: one variable; numeric for statistic=rowmean

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups to compare: one variable

parameters.name: strata
parameters.description: The stratification variables, separated by blanks (strata = sitegr1). When not given, the test has one stratum.

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: One test in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as a parameter and a visit (within = paramcd avisit)

parameters.name: statistic
parameters.description: The test: general (general association) or rowmean (the mean scores of the groups differ)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistic pval and the pattern of its printed number, such as stats = pval="X.XXXX"

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _cmh_*

macros.example:
* Tests the status at the end of the study across the groups, stratified by sex: one p value.;
%cmh(
     data   = adsl
   , var    = eosstt
   , by     = trt01a
   , strata = sex
   , label  = "Discontinued the study"
   , out    = eos_cmh
 )
* Uses the row mean score statistic for the ordered age groups: one p value.;
%cmh(
     data      = adsl
   , var       = agegr1
   , by        = trt01a
   , statistic = rowmean
   , label     = "Age group"
   , out       = agegr_cmh
 )

macros.name: columns
macros.purpose:
Returns the columns of a table: one row per column, with its N and the header that shows the N. A header is the value, a | and the N: Placebo|(N=86). %layout reads it to place each number and to label each column; the N comes from the population of n=, not from the counts of %freq.
- The columns are the values of the column variable in the results and in the population.
- They are in the order of the numeric twin of order=, else of their values; the Total is last.
- The N of a column is the number of subjects of n= with its value; the N of the Total is all subjects of n=.
- Without n= the columns have no N, and the header is the value alone.
- With page= each page has the same columns, and the N of a column is the N of its page: with page = sex on the example data, Placebo|(N=33) on the page of the males and Placebo|(N=53) on the page of the females.
macros.proven: The tables of a made-up study: the N of every column the same as that of a second program in R; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: one row per column: COL (its number: 1, 2 ...), COLVALUE (the value of var=), BIGN (the N) and HEADER (the value, a | and (N=86); %print splits a header at the |). With page=: one row per page and column, the page variable first; BIGN is the N of the page (0: no subject of the column on the page).
macros.des: The columns of a table and the N of each (PROC SUMMARY)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The stacked results (out= of %stack)

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: The population: a data set with USUBJID and the column variable, such as adsl. Each subject counts once in the N of its column. When not given, the columns have no N.

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The column variable: one variable, the first variable of by= of the statistics macros (var = trt01a)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The numeric twin of var= in n=, such as order = trt01an: the columns are in its order. When not given, the columns are in the order of their values.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: A variable of the results and of n=, such as page = sex: one page per value. The N of a column is then the N of its page. Give %layout the same page=.

parameters.name: total
parameters.description: yes: the results have the group Total (total = yes of the statistics macros); it is the last column, and its N is all subjects of n=. A text in quotes is the other name that the statistics macros gave the Total.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the data set of the columns

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _columns_*

macros.example:
* Makes the four columns with their N from adsl, the Total last, in the order of TRT01AN.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols
 )
* Gives page=sex: one row per column and sex, the N of each column on the page of its sex.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_1_1
   , n     = adsl
   , var   = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , page  = sex
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_1_1_cols
 )
* Leaves out n=: the columns have no N and come in the order of their values, the Total last.;
%columns(
     data  = t14_2_1
   , var   = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , out   = t14_2_1_cols_no_n
 )

macros.name: cox
macros.purpose: Returns the hazard ratio of pairs of groups from a Cox proportional hazards model, with its confidence limits and p-value. Use %logrank for the test of all groups together without a model, and %interaction_phreg for the test of a treatment-by-subgroup interaction. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The model has the groups, the covariates and the class factors. With strata=, each combination of the values of the strata variables is a stratum with its own baseline hazard. All pairs come from one fit: hr is the hazard ratio, lcl and ucl are its Wald confidence limits, and pval is the Wald p-value of the pair. With pvalue=logrank, pval is the log-rank test of the two groups of the pair, in the same strata (PROC LIFETEST); the hazard ratio and its limits stay those of the model. The model uses one record per subject (in each group of within=). CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR.
macros.procedure: PROC PHREG (LSMEANS); PROC LIFETEST for pvalue=logrank
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per pair and statistic: the BY variable (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), the variables of within=, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. hr is the hazard of the group over the hazard of VERSUS (a hazard ratio below 1: fewer events in the group, as its hazard is lower), lcl and ucl its confidence limits, pval its p-value. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. GROUPS is the name of the BY variable, VERSUS and the names of within=.
macros.des: The hazard ratio of pairs of groups from a Cox model (PROC PHREG)
macros.note: The ties of the library are Efron's, as in coxph of R; PROC PHREG by itself uses Breslow's.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID, the time and the censoring variable

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'TTDE')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The time: one numeric variable, such as aval

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups of the model: one character variable

parameters.name: cnsr
parameters.description: The censoring variable: one numeric variable, 0 for an event and a positive value for a censoring (the ADaM CNSR: 1, 2 ... name the reason). A missing or negative value on a record used stops the macro with an ERROR.

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: One model in each group of these variables, separated by blanks (within = sex for the levels of a subgroup). A record with a missing value of one of them is not used.

parameters.name: covars
parameters.description: The numeric covariates of the model, separated by blanks (covars = age)

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: The class factors of the model, separated by blanks (class = sitegr1)

parameters.name: strata
parameters.description: The strata of the model, separated by blanks (strata = sitegr1). When not given, the model has no strata.

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or a list of pairs separated by #: the group first, then the group it is compared with, each value in quotes ("Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low")

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01pn)

parameters.name: ties
parameters.description: The method for tied times: efron, breslow, or exact (TIES=DISCRETE of PROC PHREG, which coxph of R calls exact). discrete is accepted as another name of exact

parameters.name: pvalue
parameters.description: The p-value of each pair: wald (the Wald test of the pair in the model) or logrank (the log-rank test of the two groups of the pair, in the strata). logrank is not possible with within=

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are hr, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _cox_*

macros.example:
* Gives the hazard ratio of each pair, stratified by sex, with its limits and p value.;
%cox(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval
   , by     = trt01a
   , strata = sex
   , order  = trt01an
   , out    = ttde_hr
 )
* Gives the hazard ratio against Placebo for each sex: the rows carry SEX, for a forest plot.;
%cox(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = sex
   , pairs  = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , out    = hr_sex
 )
* Gives the hazard ratio against Placebo for each age group.;
%cox(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = agegr1
   , pairs  = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , out    = hr_age
 )
* Uses the Breslow ties, and as p value the log rank test of the two groups of each pair.;
%cox(
     data   = adttde
   , var    = aval
   , by     = trt01a
   , pairs  = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , ties   = breslow
   , pvalue = logrank
   , out    = ttde_hr_lr
 )

macros.name: csv
macros.purpose: Writes the records of a listing, or the numbers of a figure, to a CSV file. Use %ard for the numbers of a table. The first line has the names of the variables, in upper case; then one line per record, in the order of the data. The values are written with their formats, so that a second program, in SAS or R, can compare its listing or figure with this file.
macros.proven: The listings of a made-up study: the same as the listings of a second program in R; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: FILE: <out>/<folder>/<file>.csv, where <out> is the output folder that %study set: a line with the names of var=, then one line per record.
macros.des: The records of a listing as a CSV file (DATA steps)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The records: the data set of the listing, or out= of a figure macro

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The variables to write: names separated by blanks, in the order of the columns

parameters.name: folder
parameters.description: The folder in the outputs: listings or figures

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The name of the CSV file, without its extension

macros.example:
* Writes the listing as a CSV file: the names of var= in the first line, then one line per record.;
%csv(data=adae, var=trt01a usubjid aedecod astdt, file=l14_5_1)

macros.name: describe
macros.purpose: Returns the descriptive statistics of a numeric variable in each group: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum. Use %freq for the subjects of each category of a variable. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). Only the values that are not missing count. Q1, Q3 and the standard error come when stats= asks for them. The default pattern of min and max is XX, a whole number: a lab value of 3.9 prints as 4. Give min="XX.X" max="XX.X" in stats= for values with decimals.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per group and statistic: the BY variables, the variables of keep=, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. A group with no value has no row. When no record has a value, the result has no row and the log has the NOTE "No data qualified".
macros.des: Descriptive statistics of a variable in each group (PROC MEANS)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). When not given, all records are used.

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The variable to describe: one numeric variable

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one variable or several, separated by blanks. The first variable gives the columns of the table; the others give its rows, such as a parameter and a visit (by = trt01a paramcd avisit).

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Other variables to keep in the result, separated by blanks, for the names and the order of the rows (keep = param avisitn). Each gets its largest value in the group (the ID statement of PROC MEANS).

parameters.name: total
parameters.description: yes: add the group "Total", all groups of the first BY variable together. A text in quotes gives the Total another name ("All subjects"). A record with a missing group is counted in no group and not in the Total.

parameters.name: qntldef
parameters.description: The definition of the quantiles: a number from 1 to 5, as QNTLDEF= of PROC MEANS (5 is the default of SAS)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.default: n="XX" mean="XX.X" sd="XX.XX" median="XX.X" min="XX" max="XX"
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, mean, sd, median, min, max, q1, q3 and se. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: XX for n, min and max; XX.X for mean, median, q1 and q3; XX.XX for sd and se.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _describe_*

macros.example:
* Summarizes age in each group and in the Total: n, mean, SD, median, minimum and maximum.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_describe
 )
* Uses three BY variables: one row per group, parameter, visit and statistic, with PARAM kept.;
%describe(
     data  = advs
   , where = (anl01fl = 'Y')
   , var   = aval
   , by    = trt01a paramcd avisit
   , keep  = param avisitn
   , out   = vs
 )
* Adds the SE, Q1 and Q3 and calls the Total All subjects: the rows keep the order of stats=.;
%describe(
     data  = advs
   , where = (paramcd = 'WEIGHT' AND ablfl = 'Y')
   , var   = aval
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = "All subjects"
   , stats = n mean sd se median q1 q3 min="XX.X" max="XX.X"
   , label = "Weight at baseline (kg)"
   , out   = wt_describe
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the rows of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%describe(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = age
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age (years)"
   , out   = age_sex
 )

macros.name: fisher
macros.purpose: Returns the p-value of Fisher's exact test of the subjects with a record against the subjects without, between groups. Use it for an adverse event between treatments; use %chisq for the categories of a response, and %cmh for a test within strata. Every subject of denom= counts, with a record in data= or without. A subject with a missing group in denom= is not used. With exact=no the macro gives the Pearson chi-square test of the same table. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack): one row with STAT pval, or one row per group of within= with the variables of within=. GROUPS has the names of the within= variables. VALUE is missing where no test can be made (one group, or all subjects with a record, or none).
macros.des: Fisher exact test of subjects with a record against those without (PROC FREQ)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records (adverse events), with USUBJID

parameters.name: denom
parameters.description: The subjects, one row each, with USUBJID and the variable of by=: a data set, with data set options if needed, such as denom = adsl(where = (saffl = 'Y'))

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y')

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups to compare: one variable of denom=

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: One test in each group of these variables of data=, separated by blanks, such as each preferred term (within = aedecod)

parameters.name: exact
parameters.description: no: the Pearson chi-square test of the same table instead of Fisher's exact test

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistic pval and the pattern of its printed number, such as stats = pval="X.XXXX"

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _fisher_*

macros.example:
* Tests the subjects with an event against those without in each class: one p value per class.;
%fisher(
     data   = adae
   , denom  = adsl
   , where  = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = aebodsys
   , out    = soc_test
 )

macros.name: flag_first
macros.purpose: Flags the first or last record of each group, among the records that meet a condition, with Y. Use %pick to copy the value of such a record to a subject. Use %flag_if_any to flag the subjects that have any record that meets a condition. The records of a group are sorted by order=. A missing sort key sorts last. Records with equal keys keep their order. The other records get a blank flag. The rows of data= keep their order.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of the flag of the first or the last record (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: DATA: data=, changed in place: the character variable new= ($1), Y on the first (or last) record of each group among the records that meet where=, blank on the other records.
macros.des: Flag the first or last record of each group that meets a condition (PROC SORT, MERGE)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set to change in place, such as advs

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records that can be flagged: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y'). When not given, all records can be flagged.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: variables separated by blanks (by = usubjid paramcd)

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The sort keys within a group: variables separated by blanks; write descending before a key as in a BY statement (order = descending adt)

parameters.name: which
parameters.description: first or last: the record of the group that gets the flag

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: The name of the flag variable to make

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _flag_first_*

macros.name: flag_if_any
macros.purpose: Flags with Y every row of each subject that has a record in another data set that meets a condition. Use %flag_first to flag one record of each group instead of a subject. The other subjects get N, or a blank with else=blank. The rows of data= keep their order.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of a flag from a condition and from any record of a subject (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: DATA: data=, changed in place: the character variable new= ($1) on every row of a subject, Y when the subject has such a record in from=, N (or blank) when not.
macros.des: Flag the subjects with a record in another data set that meets a condition (PROC SORT)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set to change in place, such as adsl

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The data set of the records, with USUBJID, such as adae

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The condition on the records of from=, in parentheses, such as where = (aesev = 'SEVERE')

parameters.name: else
parameters.description: The value for the other subjects: N, or blank for a blank value

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: The name of the flag variable to make

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _flag_if_any_*

macros.name: forestplot
macros.purpose: Draws a forest plot of estimates in subgroups as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. It computes no statistic: it draws a result of %cox, %logistic, %rateratio, %lsmeans or %risk called with within=, so the figure and the table of the same result cannot differ. A result is the data set a statistics macro writes, one row per number. For the test of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction, use the %interaction_* macros. Each factor of within= has a heading row, with one row per level under it. The estimate is a marker and its confidence interval a bar; a line marks no difference. A ratio has a log axis (scale=log). With text=yes, the estimate and its limits are also written as text at the right. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.
macros.proven: Its known answer: made-up results, arranged by hand; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-27 (the cases of the 9 figure macros: 103 of 103 the same)
macros.output: OUT: one row per level and pair: FACTOR (the variable of within=), LEVEL (its value as printed), PAIR (the group of by= against VERSUS; blank without by=), KIND (estimate), X (the estimate), LOWER, UPPER and N (missing when the result has no statistic n). OUTPAR: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). FILE: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.
macros.des: Forest plot of results in the levels of subgroups (PROC SGPLOT)
macros.note: Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %forestplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed: the factors, levels and pairs in the order of its rows, each factor under the heading of its name. par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, estimate (with plot= only for the name over the text column), scale, text, xlabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

parameters.name: plot
parameters.description: Draw again: the out= of an earlier %forestplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=.

parameters.name: par

parameters.name: estimate

parameters.name: lower
parameters.description: The statistic of the lower limit: a value of STAT

parameters.name: upper
parameters.description: The statistic of the upper limit: a value of STAT

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: The factors: variables of the result separated by blanks, one per factor, in the order of the rows (within = sex agegr1). A row belongs to the first of them that has a value.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: A variable with the heading of each factor. When not given, the heading is the label of the variable of within=.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The group of a pair: a variable of the result. When the result has VERSUS, the pair is the group of by= against VERSUS. Each pair has its own colour.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: The scale of the x axis: log (for a ratio) or linear (for a difference)

parameters.name: text

parameters.name: xlabel
parameters.description: The label of the x axis: a text in quotes

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The line of no difference on the x axis: one value, 1 for a ratio or 0 for a difference

parameters.name: width

parameters.name: height

parameters.name: debug

* Draws the hazard ratios of each subgroup on a log scale, with the reference line at 1.;
%forestplot(

macros.name: freq
macros.purpose: Counts the subjects in each category and group, with their percent of the subjects of the group. Use %proportion when the percent needs a confidence interval, and %worst for the worst grade of each subject. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). A subject is counted once in each cell. A record with a missing group or category is not counted. The percent is of the subjects of the group in denom=. Without var=, the macro counts the subjects with any record. The name events in stats= adds the number of records of each cell.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answers: the counts and the percents of the subjects (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per group, category and statistic: the variables of by= and var=, the variables of keep=, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. Every group of denom= has every category: n = 0 when no subject has it. With levels=, the twin <V>N of each planned variable gives its place in levels=; with order=frequency, the twin of orderof= gives the rank.
macros.des: Frequencies of subjects in each group and category (PROC FREQ)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records to count, with USUBJID

parameters.name: denom
parameters.description: The subjects of each group: the N of the percent and the columns. A data set with one row per subject and the variables of by=; data set options are allowed: adsl(where=(saffl = 'Y')). When not given, the subjects of data= (without where=).

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to count: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The categories: one variable or several, separated by blanks, nested in their order (var = aebodsys aedecod: a term within its class). When not given, the macro counts the subjects with any record.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one variable or several, separated by blanks. The first variable gives the columns of the table; the others give its rows or its pages (by = trt01a sex, with page= of %layout).

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Other variables to keep with the categories for their names and order, separated by blanks. PARAM and PARAMN go with PARAMCD, AVISITN with AVISIT, any <V>N with V. Each gets the value of the first record of its category.

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: The planned categories of some variables of var=: each variable followed by its values in quotes (levels = bnrind 'LOW' 'NORMAL' 'HIGH'). A planned category shows also without a subject; a record of another category is not counted. The rows of a planned variable V follow the order given, through its twin VN (1, 2 ...) in out=, unless keep= has VN. The categories of the other variables come from the records counted.

parameters.name: total
parameters.description: yes: add the group "Total", all groups of the first BY variable together. A text in quotes gives the Total another name ("All subjects"). The first BY variable must be character.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: A percent (threshold = 5): keep only the categories with this percent of the subjects or more in at least one group (the Total counts as a group). The macro compares the percent itself, not its rounded text.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: frequency: order the rows of orderof= by their subjects, the most first, and equal counts by their value. The rank goes into the twin <V>N, and %print orders the rows by it. When not given, the rows are in the order of the values.

parameters.name: orderof
parameters.description: The variable of var= whose rows order=frequency ranks: one variable. When not given, the last variable of var=.

parameters.name: orderby
parameters.description: The group whose subjects rank the rows for order=frequency: a value of the first BY variable, in quotes (orderby = "Placebo"). When not given, all groups together, without the Total.

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, pct and events. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _freq_*

macros.example:
* Counts each sex in each group and in the Total: n and the percent of the subjects of the group.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = sex
   , by    = trt01a
   , total = yes
   , label = "Sex"
   , out   = sex_freq
 )
* Counts subjects and events of each term under its class: the percent uses the N of denom=.;
%freq(
     data  = adae
   , denom = adsl
   , where = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , var   = aebodsys aedecod
   , by    = trt01a
   , stats = n pct events
   , out   = teae
 )
* Counts the shift at Week 24 with planned levels: a level without a subject has a row of 0.;
%freq(
     data   = adlb
   , denom  = adsl
   , where  = (avisit = 'Week 24')
   , var    = paramcd bnrind anrind
   , by     = trt01a
   , levels = bnrind 'LOW' 'NORMAL' 'HIGH' anrind 'LOW' 'NORMAL' 'HIGH'
   , out    = shift
 )
* Keeps the terms that reach 5 percent in a group: AEDECODN ranks them, the most subjects first.;
%freq(
     data      = adae
   , denom     = adsl
   , where     = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , var       = aedecod
   , by        = trt01a
   , threshold = 5
   , order     = frequency
   , out       = common
 )
* Adds sex as a second BY variable: the age groups of each group and sex, for a page per sex.;
%freq(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = agegr1
   , by    = trt01a sex
   , total = yes
   , label = "Age group"
   , out   = agegr_sex
 )

macros.name: import_xpt

macros.output: FILE: one data set <out>/<member>.sas7bdat for each name of members=.
macros.des: Read SAS transport files (XPORT version 5) into SAS data sets (PROC COPY)

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: The folder of the transport files: a path without quotes

parameters.name: members
parameters.description: The names of the data sets to read: one name or several, separated by blanks (members = dm ae vs). The file of VTXC is VTXC.xpt or, when that does not exist, vtxc.xpt.
