macros.name: interaction_genmod
macros.purpose: Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a Poisson or negative binomial model of a count. Use %interaction_glm for a continuous variable, %interaction_logistic for a response, and %interaction_phreg for a time to an event. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The macro fits two models with PROC GENMOD, with the logarithm of the exposure as the offset: the groups, the covariates, the class factors and the factor; and the same model with the treatment-by-factor terms. In a negative binomial model, each fit estimates its own dispersion k. pval is the likelihood-ratio test: twice the difference of the full log likelihoods of the two fits, with the difference of the numbers of their estimated coefficients. The models use one record per subject: a record with a missing count, group or level is not used.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answers: a Poisson and a negative binomial model (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row for all groups and levels together: GROUPS (blank), BLOCK, STAT (pval), VALUE and TEXT.
macros.des: The likelihood-ratio test of the treatment-by-factor interaction, counts (PROC GENMOD)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (ittfl = 'Y')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The count: one numeric variable, such as the number of events of each subject

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups of the model, the treatment: one variable

parameters.name: factor
parameters.description: The factor of the subgroups: one variable whose values are its levels (factor = sex)

parameters.name: exposure
parameters.description: The exposure of each subject: a numeric variable, or an expression of it (exposure = trtdurd / 365.25). It must be above 0, because the offset is its logarithm.

parameters.name: covars
parameters.description: The numeric covariates of the model, separated by blanks (covars = base)

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: The other class factors of the model, separated by blanks (class = sitegr1)

parameters.name: dist
parameters.description: The distribution of the count: poisson or negbin (nb is accepted as another name of negbin)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistic with its pattern of the printed number: pval

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _interaction_genmod_*

macros.example:
* Tests the treatment by sex interaction of the event counts in a negative binomial model.;
%interaction_genmod(
     data     = adsl
   , where    = (trtdurd > 0)
   , var      = teaecnt
   , by       = trt01a
   , factor   = sex
   , exposure = trtdurd / 365.25
   , dist     = negbin
   , label    = "Sex"
   , out      = ae_int
 )

macros.name: interaction_glm
macros.purpose: Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a linear model of a continuous variable. Use %interaction_logistic for a response, %interaction_genmod for a count with its exposure, and %interaction_phreg for a time to an event. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The model has the groups, the covariates, the class factors, the factor and the treatment-by-factor terms. pval is the Type III F test of the treatment-by-factor terms (PROC GLM). For this term of the highest order, the test is the same as the F test of the model with the terms against the model without them. The model uses one record per subject: a record with a missing value, group or level is not used.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row for all groups and levels together: GROUPS (blank), BLOCK, STAT (pval), VALUE and TEXT.
macros.des: The F test of the treatment-by-factor interaction in a linear model (PROC GLM)

macros.name: interaction_phreg
macros.purpose: Returns the p-value of the treatment-by-subgroup interaction in a Cox model of a time to an event. Use %interaction_glm for a continuous variable, %interaction_logistic for a response, and %interaction_genmod for a count with its exposure. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The macro fits two models with PROC PHREG, in the strata of strata=: the groups, the covariates, the class factors and the factor; and the same model with the treatment-by-factor terms. pval is the likelihood-ratio test: the difference of the likelihood-ratio chi-squares of the two fits (twice the difference of the log partial likelihoods), with the difference of their degrees of freedom. The models use one record per subject: a record with a missing time, group or level is not used. CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row for all groups and levels together: GROUPS (blank), BLOCK, STAT (pval), VALUE and TEXT.
macros.des: The likelihood-ratio test of the treatment-by-factor interaction (PROC PHREG)

macros.name: km
macros.purpose: Returns the Kaplan-Meier summary of a time in each group: subjects, events, the median time and its confidence limits. Use %kmplot to draw the curve, and %table_tte for the whole table of a time to event in one call. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The statistics are n (the subjects), events, median, lcl and ucl. The limits of the median are those of Brookmeyer and Crowley, from PROC LIFETEST. A median or a limit that the curve does not reach has a missing VALUE and the TEXT NE (not estimable). Without time=, lcl and ucl are the limits of the median. With time=, surv is the survival at that time in percent, and lcl and ucl are the limits of that survival, in percent, not of the median; the default stats= has no surv, so give stats= with surv to show it. A record with a missing time or a missing group is not used. CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answers: the median and the percent without an event at a time (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per group and statistic: the BY variable, GROUPS, BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies, the result has no row and the log has the NOTE "No data qualified".
macros.des: The Kaplan-Meier summary of a time in each group (PROC LIFETEST)
macros.note: The macro does not give the number at risk at given times: %kmplot draws it and keeps it in its out= data set.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: one record per subject, with the time and the censoring variable

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'TTDE')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The time: one numeric variable, such as aval

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one variable

parameters.name: cnsr
parameters.description: The censoring variable: one numeric variable, 0 for an event and a positive value for a censoring (the ADaM CNSR: 1, 2 ... name the reason). A missing or negative value on a record used stops the macro with an ERROR.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: One time at which to give the survival: a number, such as time = 180. When not given, the result has no survival.

parameters.name: conftype
parameters.description: The transformation of the confidence interval: linear, log or loglog, as CONFTYPE= of PROC LIFETEST (the default of PROC LIFETEST itself is loglog)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, events, median, lcl, ucl and, with time=, surv. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _km_*

macros.example:
* Gives n, events, the median and its limits of each group: NE is a median not reached.;
%km(
     data  = adttde
   , var   = aval
   , by    = trt01a
   , label = "Time to the first skin event (days)"
   , out   = ttde_km
 )
* Gives the percent of subjects alive at day 182 and its limits, with the patterns of stats=.;
%km(
     data  = adtte
   , where = (paramcd = 'OS')
   , var   = aval
   , by    = trt01p
   , time  = 182
   , stats = n="XX" events="XX" surv="XX.X" lcl="XX.X" ucl="XX.X"
   , out   = os_km
 )
* Uses conftype=loglog: only the lower limit of Low Dose changes, 51 to 48.;
%km(
     data     = adttde
   , var      = aval
   , by       = trt01a
   , conftype = loglog
   , out      = ttde_kmll
 )
* Uses a 90 percent level: on these data the limits of the median stay as at 95 percent.;
%km(
     data  = adttde
   , var   = aval
   , by    = trt01a
   , level = 0.90
   , out   = ttde_km90
 )

macros.name: kmplot
macros.purpose: Draws the Kaplan-Meier curve of each group as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. Use %km for the Kaplan-Meier estimates in a table; %kmplot computes its own curve with PROC LIFETEST. The survival is in percent, drawn as steps, with a mark at each censored time. Under the axis is the number at risk at each tick: the subjects whose time is that tick or later. With median=yes, the plot also shows the median time of each group and its confidence interval (NE: not reached). A record with a missing time, group or panel is not used. CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.
macros.procedure: PROC LIFETEST, PROC SUMMARY, PROC SGPANEL
macros.proven: Its known answer: the survival and the number at risk, worked out by hand; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-27 (the cases of the 9 figure macros: 103 of 103 the same)
macros.output: OUT: one row per number drawn, with the variables of panel= and by=, KIND, X, Y, LOWER, UPPER, N and CENSORED. In a row of KIND curve, X is a time (0 and each time with an event or a censoring), Y the survival in percent after it, and CENSORED is 1 when a subject is censored at it. In a row of KIND atrisk, X is a tick and N the number at risk. In a row of KIND median, X is the median and LOWER and UPPER its limits (missing: not reached). OUTPAR: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). FILE: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.
macros.des: Kaplan-Meier curves with the number at risk (PROC LIFETEST, PROC SGPANEL)
macros.note: Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %kmplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed. par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, atrisk, median, level (with plot= only for the heading of the medians), xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table. With plot=, the ticks are the X of the rows of KIND atrisk.

macros.name: layout
macros.purpose:
Returns the display data set of a table: one row per printed line and one column per group. %print prints it; %table runs %columns, %ard, %layout and %print in one call. The display data set is the table as the shells show it: each row a printed line, each cell a text. %layout computes nothing: every number is the TEXT of a result. The rows:
- Each block starts with its label, with a blank row between two blocks.
- The levels of the groups other than the column variable are indented by two blanks each: a term under its class, a visit under its parameter, vs B under A.
- The levels are in the order of their numeric twin (AVISITN for AVISIT, PARAMN for PARAMCD: the name with an N added), else of their values. A level of PARAMCD shows its PARAM.
- A frequency block (only the statistics n, pct, events, lcl and ucl) has one line per category. Any other block has one line per kind of statistic, by the line table below.
- The p-value of each category (a test of each term, in a block of the same label) stands in the row of its category.
- A result has at most four groups besides the column variable and the page variable.
The columns:
- C1 ... Cn: one column per group, with its header and N from %columns.
- C99, All groups: the numbers of a result without the column variable, such as a p-value of all groups.
The line table: each line by its order and its label, then its template.
- line 0 (a category of a frequency block): {n} {pct} {events} ({lcl}, {ucl})
- line 1 (n): {n}
- line 2 (Events): {events}
- line 2.5 (Patient-years): {exposure}
- line 3 (Mean (SD)): {mean} ({sd}) [{se}]. With se and no sd the label is Mean (SE); with both, Mean (SD) [SE].
- line 4 (Median): {median}
- line 5 (Q1, Q3): {q1}, {q3}
- line 6 (Min, Max): {min}, {max}
- line 7 (LS mean (SE)): {lsmean} ({lsmean_se})
- line 8 (Difference (SE)): {diff} ({diff_se})
- line 9 (the estimate, labelled by its STAT): {estimate}. The labels: STAT hr: Hazard ratio; STAT or: Odds ratio; STAT irr: Rate ratio; STAT rd: Risk difference; STAT rr: Relative risk; STAT rate: Rate per 100 patient-years; STAT estimate: Estimate.
- line 10 (Confidence interval): ({lcl}, {ucl})
- line 11 (p-value): {pval}
- line 11.5 (Adjusted p-value): {padj}
- line 12 (any other STAT, labelled by its name): {value}
In a template:
- A part that is missing leaves out its piece with its brackets or its comma: a confidence interval without its upper limit prints the lower limit alone.
- A TEXT that has the brackets of its piece already is not bracketed twice.
- The counts of a frequency block are right aligned to the widest count.
The setup (setup=):
- The global macro variable keeps the parameters of %print for out=: data=, by=row, var=c:, together=grp and label=row=" " with the labels of label=; also page=, rows=, file= and nodata= when they are given to %layout. A NOTE in the log shows it.
- %print(&name.) prints the display data set again after a change. A parameter that is not in the setup is added after it: %print(&name., file=...).
- A parameter that is in the setup cannot be given again, as SAS stops a call that has a keyword twice: give it to %layout, or write the whole %print call.
When data= has no row, the display data set has no row, and %print prints the text of nodata=.
macros.procedure: DATA steps, PROC FORMAT, PROC SORT, PROC TRANSPOSE
macros.proven: The 12 tables of a made-up study, each with a clean log, also as the code the macros wrote, run without the macros; its test cases of setup=; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12. The 12 tables of the CDISC pilot study (the p-value of each term in Table 14.5.2), 2026-11-13
macros.output: OUT: the display data set, one row per printed line: GRP (the rows that stay on one page: a block, or a level of its first group; a row of a value of all groups, such as a p-value in C99 only, has the GRP of the rows of its block before it), ROW (the label of the line, indented, with the format $CHARw.), C1 ... Cn (the cells, labelled with the header of their column) and C99 (All groups: only when a result has a number without the column variable). With page=: also the page variable (with its format of format=) and HEAD_C1 ... HEAD_Cn, the header of each column on its page; C1 ... Cn are then labelled with the column value. SETUP: with setup=, the global macro variable of that name.
macros.des: The display data set of a table: its rows and a column per group (DATA steps)

parameters.name: columns

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The column variable of the results: the same variable as var= of %columns

parameters.name: page

parameters.name: format

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Column labels for %print: name="text" pairs, separated by blanks. They go into the setup after row=" ".

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: The rows of a page for %print (rows= of %print): a whole number. It goes into the setup.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The output of %print: a path without its extension (file= of %print). It goes into the setup.

parameters.name: nodata
parameters.description: The text that %print prints when there is no row (nodata= of %print). It goes into the setup.

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: The name of a global macro variable that keeps the %print call of out=: a SAS name that does not start with SYS or SPL_. When not given, no setup is made.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the display data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _layout_*

* Makes the display data set: one row per printed line, one column per group, sex by its labels.;
%layout(
     data    = t14_2_1
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , var     = trt01a
   , format  = sex $sexf.
   , file    = &spl_out./tlf/t14_2_1
   , setup   = t14_2_1_print
   , out     = t14_2_1_display
 )
* Makes one page per sex: SEX and HEAD_C1 to HEAD_C4 hold the page and the N of each column on it.;

     data    = t14_1_1
   , columns = t14_1_1_cols
   , var     = trt01a
   , page    = sex
   , format  = sex $sexf.
   , file    = &spl_out./tlf/t14_1_1
   , setup   = t14_1_1_print
   , out     = t14_1_1_display
 )
* Puts label= and rows= into the setup: the last column is labelled p value, 30 rows a page.;
%layout(
     data    = t14_2_1
   , columns = t14_2_1_cols
   , var     = trt01a
   , format  = sex $sexf.
   , label   = c99="p-value"
   , rows    = 30
   , file    = &spl_out./tlf/t14_2_1_label
   , setup   = t14_2_1_label_print
   , out     = t14_2_1_label_display
 )

%print(&t14_2_1_label_print.)
* Counts the severe events of the subjects under 50: there is none, so the result has no row.;
%freq(

  , var   = aedecod
  , by    = trt01a

)

%print(&t_sev50_print.)

It computes nothing: use it for values computed before (the LS means of %lsmeans or %mmrm by visit, a rate by month), and %meanplot to compute the mean of the records. The interval of lower= and upper= is drawn as error bars, with the groups a little apart on the x axis, or as a band. A row with a missing x, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.

macros.name: locf
macros.purpose:
Adds last-observation-carried-forward records (DTYPE = 'LOCF') to the analysis windows in which a group has no analysed record. Use %windows first: it gives each record the AVISITN of its window. The rule:
- An analysed record has flag= equal to 'Y' and a window after baseline.
- For each window, from the second window after baseline on, that has no analysed record of the group, the macro copies the last analysed record before it and moves the copy to that window.
- Baseline is not carried forward, and the first window after baseline is not filled.
The new records get the window variables of their window and DTYPE = 'LOCF'; the other records get a blank DTYPE.
macros.procedure: PROC SORT, a DATA step (SET POINT=)
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of the value carried into a visit without one (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: DATA: data=, changed in place: the new records are added, and all records are sorted by the groups, AVISITN and DTYPE.
macros.des: Last observation carried forward into the analysis windows, as new records (PROC SORT)

parameters.name: by

parameters.name: flag

parameters.name: day

parameters.name: debug

macros.name: logistic
macros.purpose: Returns the odds ratios of pairs of groups from a logistic regression, with their Wald confidence limits and p-values. Use %risk for a risk difference, relative risk or odds ratio from the 2 x 2 table of a pair, without a model. The model is PROC LOGISTIC of a response with two values: the probability of the event of event= on the groups, the class factors and the covariates, one record per subject (the first with a response). All pairs come from one fit. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per pair and statistic: the group in the by= variable, the group it is compared with in VERSUS, and the variables of within=. or is the odds of the event of event= in the group over the odds in VERSUS, adjusted for the covariates and the class factors (an odds ratio above 1: the event is more likely in the group), lcl and ucl its Wald confidence limits, pval its p-value. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. GROUPS is the by= variable, VERSUS and the within= variables.
macros.des: The odds ratio of pairs of groups from a logistic regression (PROC LOGISTIC)
macros.note: The iterations go on until no parameter changes by more than 1E-10 (XCONV=). PROC LOGISTIC alone stops at a relative gradient of 1E-8. So the estimate is the maximum to the digits R gives: the odds ratio 7 of a 2 x 2 table is 7, where GCONV=1E-10 gave 6.9999907.

parameters.name: where

parameters.name: by

parameters.name: within

parameters.name: covars

parameters.name: class

parameters.name: debug

macros.name: logrank
macros.purpose: Returns the p-value of the log-rank test that compares the time to an event between the groups. Use %km for the medians of the groups, and %cox for a hazard ratio with its confidence interval. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The test uses one record per subject: when a subject has several records, the first one in the order of USUBJID is used, so where= must select one parameter. With strata=, the test is the stratified log-rank test: each combination of the values of the strata variables is one stratum (STRATA strata / GROUP=by of PROC LIFETEST). With only one group there is no test, and the p-value is missing. CNSR 0 is an event and any positive value is a censoring, as in ADaM, where the value names the reason of the censoring: a CNSR of 2 is censored as 1 is. A record used with a missing or negative CNSR stops the macro with an ERROR.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row for all groups together: GROUPS (blank), BLOCK, STAT (pval), VALUE and TEXT.
macros.des: The log-rank test of a time between groups (PROC LIFETEST)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID, the time and the censoring variable

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'TTDE')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The time: one numeric variable, such as aval

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups to compare: one variable

parameters.name: cnsr

macros.name: lsmeans
macros.purpose: The ANCOVA of the groups: returns the differences of the LS means of pairs of groups in a linear model, with confidence limits and p-values. Use %ancova for the test of one numeric term (a dose response), and %mmrm for repeated visits of a subject. The model is PROC MIXED without a random effect (least squares): the covariates, the class factors and the groups, one record per subject (the first with a value; when where= leaves a second record of a subject, the log has a NOTE with their number). Give a where= that leaves one record per subject, such as one parameter at one visit with anl01fl = 'Y'; otherwise each subject has the first of its records in the order of data=, whichever it is. The LS mean of each group comes when stats= asks for it. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack). A row of a difference has the group in the by= variable and the group it is compared with in VERSUS: diff is the LS mean of the group minus the LS mean of VERSUS (a negative diff: a smaller LS mean in the group), diff_se its standard error, lcl and ucl its confidence limits, pval the p-value of the test that it is 0. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. A row of an LS mean has VERSUS blank. GROUPS is the by= variable, VERSUS and the within= variables.
macros.des: The differences of the LS means of pairs of groups in a linear model (PROC MIXED)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set, with USUBJID

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12')

parameters.name: var

parameters.name: by

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: One model in each group of these variables, separated by blanks (within = paramcd)

parameters.name: covars

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: The class factors besides the groups: variables separated by blanks (class = sex)

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low"

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01pn)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl, pval, lsmean, lsmean_se, lsmean_lcl and lsmean_ucl. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out

parameters.name: debug

macros.example:
* Gives the difference of the LS means of every pair at Week 12, adjusted for baseline and sex.;
%lsmeans(

   , var    = chg

macros.name: meanplot
macros.purpose: Draws the mean or median of each group by visit as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. It computes the statistic from the records; use %lineplot for values computed before (the LS means of %mmrm by visit) and %profileplot for the line of each subject. The error bars are the SE, the SD or the confidence interval of the mean, or Q1 and Q3 of the median. The points of a group are joined by a line, and the groups stand a little apart on the x axis so that their bars do not overlap. With ntable=yes, the n of each visit and group is shown under the axis. The quantiles are those of PROC MEANS with QNTLDEF=5 (R quantile type 2). A record with a missing value, visit, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.
macros.proven: Its known answer: the means, SE, SD and limits, worked out by hand; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-27 (the cases of the 9 figure macros: 103 of 103 the same)
macros.output: OUT: one row per panel, group and visit: the variables of panel= and by=, KIND (mean or median), X (the visit), Y (the statistic), LOWER and UPPER (the ends of the error bar; missing for se, sd and ci when there is one value) and N. OUTPAR: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). FILE: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.
macros.des: Mean or median by visit with error bars (PROC MEANS, PROC SGPANEL)
macros.note: Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %meanplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed (error bars where LOWER has a value). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, connect, ntable, xformat, xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

macros.name: merge_subject
macros.purpose: Copies variables from a data set with one row per subject to every row of that subject, matched by USUBJID. Use %pick when the other data set has more rows per subject and one of them gives the value. The rows of data= keep their order. A subject that from= does not have gets missing values. The macro stops with an ERROR when from= has two rows of one subject, or when a variable of vars= is not in from=.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of the variables copied from the subjects and from a period (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: DATA: data=, changed in place: the variables of vars= added to every row, with the values of the subject in from=. A subject not in from= gets missing values.
macros.des: Copy variables from another data set by subject (PROC SORT, MERGE)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set to change in place, such as adsl or adae

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The data set to copy from: one row per subject, with USUBJID

parameters.name: debug

macros.name: mmrm
macros.purpose: Returns the differences of the LS means of pairs of groups at one visit from a repeated measures mixed model. Use %lsmeans for one record per subject, and %ancova for the test of one numeric term. The model is PROC MIXED with a REPEATED statement: one record per subject and visit (the first with a value). When the covariance structure of type= does not converge, the macro tries the structures of fallback= in their order. The log names the structure used, in a NOTE such as "[mmrm] The covariance structure TYPE=un converged." (a structure that did not converge has its own NOTE, and the WARNING lines of PROC MIXED of that fit are not used). The macro adds visit= to the class factors: class= needs only the others. The LS mean of each group at the visit comes when stats= asks for it. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), as in %lsmeans. A row of a difference has the group in the by= variable and the group it is compared with in VERSUS: diff is the LS mean of the group at the visit of at= minus the LS mean of VERSUS at that visit (a negative diff: a smaller LS mean in the group), diff_se its standard error, lcl and ucl its confidence limits, pval the p-value of the test that it is 0. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. A row of an LS mean has VERSUS blank. GROUPS is the by= variable and VERSUS. When no structure converges, the macro stops with an ERROR and writes no result.
macros.des: The mixed model for repeated measures: LS means and differences at a visit (PROC MIXED)
macros.note: The model is fitted by iteration: another program gives the same numbers to about five digits, not to the last one. A structure may converge in one program and not in the other. On visits that are very closely correlated, PROC MIXED stops AR(1) with an infinite likelihood where the R twin of this macro (mmrm() of the R package sapling, a separate product) converges, so the same call may use the next structure of fallback= in SAS. The NOTE "[mmrm] The covariance structure TYPE=... converged" names the structure used. The WARNING lines of a fit that did not converge are followed by a NOTE that says so.

parameters.name: data

parameters.name: where

parameters.name: visit

parameters.name: class

parameters.name: subject
parameters.description: The subject: one variable

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The fixed effects: the MODEL statement after the equal sign. It must have the term of the groups by visit: model = base trt01p avisit trt01p*avisit.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The covariance structure: TYPE= of REPEATED (un, cs, ar(1), toep ...)

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: Other covariance structures to try in their order when one does not converge, separated by blanks (fallback = toep cs)

parameters.name: ddfm
parameters.description: The degrees of freedom: DDFM= of MODEL (bw is between-within, kr is Kenward-Roger)

parameters.name: method

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low"

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01pn)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl, pval, lsmean and lsmean_se. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out

parameters.name: debug

%mmrm(

   , var      = chg
   , by       = trt01p
   , visit    = avisit
   , at       = "Week 24"
   , model    = base trt01p avisit trt01p*avisit base*avisit
   , type     = un

   , out      = sbp_mmrm
 )

macros.name: print
macros.purpose:
Prints a table or a listing with one PROC REPORT into an RTF file and a monospace listing file. It prints a table from its display data set (%layout), and a listing from its records; %table runs %columns, %ard, %layout and %print in one call.
- The BY columns come first, and a repeated value is shown once. The VAR columns follow: numbers right aligned, text left aligned as written (its leading blanks kept).
- A text column of var= wider than 40 characters wraps at a width of 40.
- The header of a column is its pair of label=, else its HEAD_X variable on the page (with page=), else the label of the variable. A | in a header splits it into lines.
- ODS wraps and pages the RTF. The rows of one value of together= stay on one page of the listing when they fit in rows=; a group that does not fit in what is left of a page starts a new page.
- A table that is too wide for a page goes on in a second part, and the last BY column is repeated there.
- With page=, each value of the page variable gets its own pages, in the same two files, under a BY statement, so that a title can name the value (OPTIONS NOBYLINE and TITLE2 "Sex: #BYVAL1").
- With no row, the report has one row: the text of nodata=.
The setup of %layout (setup=) holds the parameters of a table: %print(&name.) prints its display data set again after a change. A parameter that is not in the setup is added after it: %print(&name., file=...). SAS stops a call that has a parameter twice: change that parameter in %layout.
macros.proven: Its 18 test cases (each with a clean log and the files it is about) and the tables and listings of a made-up study (12 of 12, also as the code the macros wrote, run without the macros); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: FILE: <file>.rtf (style journal, landscape) and <file>.lst (the LISTING destination), under the titles and footnotes of the program. With page=: the pages of each value, in the order of the rows.
macros.des: Print a table or a listing into RTF and a monospace listing (PROC REPORT)

parameters.name: by

parameters.description: The other columns, in the order of the print: variables separated by blanks. A list such as c: or c1-c5 is allowed.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: A variable: each value starts a new page, and #BYVAL1 in a title prints the value. A variable HEAD_X gives the header of the column X on the page of its row.

parameters.name: together
parameters.description: A variable: the rows of one value stay on one page, such as together = grp of %layout

parameters.name: label

parameters.name: rows

parameters.name: file

parameters.name: nodata
parameters.description: The text printed when there is no row

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _print_*

A record with a missing visit, value, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.
macros.proven: Its known answer: the values and the means, worked out by hand; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-27 (the cases of the 9 figure macros: 103 of 103 the same)

KIND is subject for a value of a subject, or mean for the mean of a group (the subject is then blank); N is the number of values of a mean. OUTPAR: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). FILE: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.

These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

parameters.name: xformat

macros.name: proportion
macros.purpose: Returns the percent of subjects in each category and group, with its confidence interval by a method you name. Use %freq for counts and percents without an interval. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The statistics are n, pct, and lcl and ucl: the limits of the interval, in percent like pct. A subject is counted once in each category. The percent is of the subjects of the group in denom=. The interval comes from the BINOMIAL option of PROC FREQ.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per group, category and statistic: the variables of by= and var=, GROUPS (by= and var=), BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies and levels= is not given, the result has no row.
macros.des: The percent of subjects in each category and group with its interval (PROC FREQ)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records, with USUBJID

parameters.name: denom
parameters.description: The subjects of the percent: a data set with one row per subject and the variable of by=. When not given, the subjects of data= (without where=).

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The category: one variable

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one variable, the columns of the table

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: The planned categories: the variable, then its values in quotes (levels = avalc 'CR' 'PR'). A planned category without a subject shows with n = 0.

parameters.name: ci
parameters.description: The method of the interval: clopper-pearson (the exact interval, CL=EXACT; exact is another name for it), wilson (the score interval, CL=WILSON), wald (CL=WALD) or agresti-coull (CL=AGRESTICOULL)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1 (level = 0.90)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, pct, lcl and ucl. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _proportion_*

macros.example:
* Gives the percent that completed and that discontinued, each with its Clopper Pearson limits.;
%proportion(

   , ci     = clopper-pearson

 )
* Gives the percent of the best responses CR and PR of the N of denom=, with Wilson limits.;
%proportion(
     data   = adrs
   , denom  = adsl

   , var    = avalc
   , by     = trt01a
   , levels = avalc 'CR' 'PR'
   , ci     = wilson
   , out    = bor_ci
 )

macros.name: rate
macros.purpose:
Returns the exposure-adjusted incidence rate of each group, with its exact Poisson confidence limits. Use %freq for the percent of subjects with an event, and %rateratio to compare the rates of two groups. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The statistics:
- n: the subjects with a record (PROC FREQ); events: every record
- exposure: the sum of the exposure of the subjects of the group in denom= (PROC MEANS)
- rate: n (or events with count=events) divided by the exposure, times per=
- lcl, ucl: the exact Poisson limits, the chi-square quantiles (CINV) of 2n and 2(n + 1) degrees of freedom, halved, divided by the exposure, times per=
macros.proven: Checked against its known answers: the rate of the subjects with an event and the rate of the events (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per group and statistic: the variable of by=, GROUPS (by=), BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. Every group of denom= has its rows: n = 0 when no subject of it has a record.
macros.des: The exposure-adjusted incidence rate of each group, exact Poisson limits (PROC FREQ)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records of the events, with USUBJID

parameters.name: denom
parameters.description: The subjects of the groups with their exposure: a data set with one row per subject, USUBJID and the variable of by=

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y')

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one variable, in data= and in denom=

parameters.name: exposure
parameters.description: The exposure of a subject: a numeric variable of denom=, or an expression of its variables (exposure = trtdur / 365.25 gives years)

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: What the rate counts: subjects (the subjects with a record, each once) or events (every record)

parameters.name: per
parameters.description: The units of exposure of the rate: a number (per = 1000 gives the rate per 1000 patient-years). The row label of %layout reads "Rate per 100 patient-years"; with another per=, change LABEL in the display data set.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1 (level = 0.90)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are n, events, exposure, rate, lcl and ucl. When not given: n (events with count=events), exposure, rate, lcl and ucl. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _rate_*

macros.example:
* Gives the subjects with an event per 100 patient years, with the exposure and the limits.;
%rate(
     data     = adae
   , denom    = adsl(WHERE=(trtdurd > 0))
   , where    = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , by       = trt01a
   , exposure = trtdurd / 365.25
   , out      = ae_rate
 )
* Counts the events, not the subjects, with count=events: a subject adds each of its events.;
%rate(
     data     = adae
   , denom    = adsl(WHERE=(trtdurd > 0))
   , where    = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , by       = trt01a
   , exposure = trtdurd / 365.25
   , count    = events
   , out      = ae_events
 )
* Gives the rate of severe events per 1000 patient years with per=1000.;
%rate(
     data     = adae
   , denom    = adsl(WHERE=(trtdurd > 0))
   , where    = (trtemfl = 'Y' AND aesev = 'SEVERE')
   , by       = trt01a
   , exposure = trtdurd / 365.25
   , per      = 1000
   , out      = ae_rate1000
 )

macros.name: rateratio
macros.purpose: Returns the rate ratios of pairs of groups from a Poisson or negative binomial model, with confidence limits and p-values. Use %rate for the rate of each group without a model. The model is PROC GENMOD of a count with the logarithm of the exposure as the offset, on the groups, the covariates and the class factors, one record per subject (the first with a count). The dispersion k of a negative binomial model is estimated by maximum likelihood. All pairs come from one fit. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.proven: Checked against its known answers: a Poisson and a negative binomial model (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per pair and statistic: the group in the by= variable, the group it is compared with in VERSUS, and the variables of within=. irr is the rate of the count per unit of exposure in the group over that rate in VERSUS, adjusted for the covariates and the class factors (a rate ratio above 1: more events per unit of exposure in the group), lcl and ucl its confidence limits, pval its p-value. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. GROUPS is the by= variable, VERSUS and the within= variables.
macros.des: The rate ratio of pairs of groups, Poisson or negative binomial model (PROC GENMOD)
macros.note: The standard errors of a negative binomial model are those of PROC GENMOD: the observed information of the coefficients and the dispersion together. The R twin of this macro (rateratio() of the R package sapling, a separate product) computes the same.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set, with USUBJID: one record per subject

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtdurd > 0)

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The count: one numeric variable (var = teaecnt)

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups of the model: one character variable

parameters.name: exposure
parameters.description: The exposure of each subject: a numeric variable, or an expression of variables of data=, such as exposure = trtdurd / 365.25 for years. A subject with an exposure of 0 or less is not used in the model.

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: One model in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as the levels of a subgroup (within = sex)

parameters.name: covars
parameters.description: The covariates: numeric variables separated by blanks (covars = age)

parameters.name: class
parameters.description: The class factors besides the groups: variables separated by blanks (class = sex)

parameters.name: dist
parameters.description: The distribution of the count: poisson, or negbin (also nb) for the negative binomial

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low"

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01an)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level of the limits: a number between 0 and 1

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. The names are irr, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _rateratio_*

macros.example:
* Compares the event counts in a negative binomial model: STAT irr is the rate ratio.;
%rateratio(
     data     = adsl
   , where    = (trtdurd > 0)
   , var      = teaecnt
   , by       = trt01a
   , exposure = trtdurd / 365.25
   , dist     = negbin
   , order    = trt01an
   , out      = ae_rr
 )

macros.name: relchange
macros.purpose:
Returns new records with the change from the record before, relative to the normal range, flagged in ANRIND. Each new record compares a value with the value of the record before it in its group (by=, sorted by order=): the change is divided by half the width of the normal range, so 1 is a change as large as half the range, and limit=1 flags a change larger than half the normal range as abnormal. For each record read, the new record has:
- PARAMCD: prefix= before the code of the record
- AVAL: (value - the value of the record before) / ((upper limit - lower limit) / 2), rounded to digits= decimals
- ANRIND: H when AVAL is above limit=, L when it is below -limit=, N between, blank when AVAL is missing
AVAL is missing on the first record of a group, on a record with no AVISITN, and when a value or a limit is missing or the upper limit is not above the lower one. For the change from baseline (CHG = AVAL - BASE), use %baseline and a DATA step.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of the relative change (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: one new record for each record read, sorted by by= and order=, with the variables of data=. The limits and the variables of reset= are missing. PARAMCD keeps its length in data=, so it must be long enough for the new codes (the generated programs give it the length of the specification, which lists them).
macros.des: New records of the change from the record before, relative to the normal range (LAG)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set, such as adlb; it is not changed

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to read: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'ALT'). The record before is one of these records.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The numeric variable of the measured value, such as lbstresn

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: variables separated by blanks. The first record of a group has no record before.

parameters.name: lo
parameters.description: The numeric variable of the lower limit of the normal range

parameters.name: hi
parameters.description: The numeric variable of the upper limit of the normal range

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The variables that sort the records of a group and so give the record before, separated by blanks. A missing value sorts first.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: The text put before PARAMCD in the new records, without quotes

parameters.name: digits
parameters.description: The number of decimals of AVAL

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The limit of ANRIND, in half ranges: H above limit=, L below -limit=. The value 1 is half the normal range.

parameters.name: reset
parameters.default: BASE CHG BNRIND R2A1LO R2A1HI BR2A1LO BR2A1HI
parameters.description: The variables that are set missing on the new records, separated by blanks; a variable that data= does not have is skipped

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the data set of the new records

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _relchange_*

macros.example:
* Adds a record per value: its change from the record before, relative to half the normal range.;
%relchange(
     data  = adlb
   , where = (paramcd = 'ALT' AND MISSING(dtype))
   , value = lbstresn
   , lo    = anrlo
   , hi    = anrhi
   , out   = alt_rel
 )

macros.name: risk
macros.purpose:
Returns the risk difference, relative risk or odds ratio of pairs of groups, with its confidence interval and p-value. Use %logistic for an odds ratio adjusted for covariates in a model, and %fisher for only the p-value of an adverse event. For each pair the macro makes the 2 x 2 table of the two groups (the group first) by the event of event= against the rest, one record per subject, with PROC FREQ. measure= gives the estimate:
- rd: the risk difference, with the interval of ci=
- rr: the relative risk, with the Wald interval of its logarithm
- or: the odds ratio, with the Wald interval of its logarithm
The p-value is that of Pearson's chi-square test without continuity correction. With strata= the macro gives the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference (COMMONRISKDIFF, CL=MH) and the p-value of the CMH test. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack).
macros.procedure: PROC FREQ (RISKDIFF, RELRISK, CHISQ; COMMONRISKDIFF, CMH)
macros.proven: Checked against its known answers: the risk difference, the relative risk, the odds ratio, and the risk difference of each term of an adverse event table (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per pair and statistic: the group in the by= variable, the group it is compared with in VERSUS, and the variables of within=. The risk of a group is its subjects with the event of event= over its subjects in the records used. With measure=rd, rd is the risk of the group minus the risk of VERSUS, a difference of two proportions (0.25: 25 percentage points more in the group); with strata=, the Mantel-Haenszel estimate of that difference. With measure=rr, rr is the risk of the group over the risk of VERSUS; with measure=or, or is the odds of the event in the group over the odds in VERSUS. lcl and ucl are the limits of the estimate, pval its p-value. With pairs=all the group is the later one in the order of order=. GROUPS is the by= variable, VERSUS and the within= variables.
macros.des: The risk difference, relative risk or odds ratio of pairs of groups (PROC FREQ)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set, with USUBJID: one record per subject, or per subject and term with within=

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (saffl = 'Y')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The response: one variable with two values, numeric or character

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: The value of var= that is the event, in quotes (event = "DISCONTINUED")

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one character variable

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: One comparison in each group of these variables, separated by blanks, such as each term of an adverse event table with the flags of %termflags (within = aebodsys aedecod)

parameters.name: strata
parameters.description: The strata of the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference: variables separated by blanks. Only with measure=rd.

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: The pairs of groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (or of the values). Or the pairs separated by #, each the group first and then the group it is compared with, a value with a blank or a hyphen in quotes: pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low"

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01an)

parameters.name: measure
parameters.description: The estimate of the group against the group it is compared with: rd, the risk difference, a difference of two proportions between -1 and 1 (0.25 is 25 percentage points), not of percents; rr, the relative risk, the ratio of the two risks; or or, the odds ratio, the ratio of the two odds. A ratio has no unit.

parameters.name: ci
parameters.description: The interval of a risk difference: wald, newcombe, miettinen-nurminen (CL=MN), agresti-caffo (CL=AC) or mh, the interval of Mantel and Haenszel, which needs strata=; with strata= the interval is always mh, whatever ci= says

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level of the interval: a number between 0 and 1

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with the pattern of its printed number, separated by blanks. When not given: rd="X.XXX" lcl="X.XXX" ucl="X.XXX" pval="X.XXX"; for measure=rr or or, rr="XX.XX" or or="XX.XX" with lcl="XX.XX" ucl="XX.XX" pval="X.XXX". A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _risk_*

macros.example:
* Gives the risk difference of discontinuation of each pair, its Newcombe limits and p value.;
%risk(
     data  = adsl
   , var   = eosstt
   , event = "DISCONTINUED"
   , by    = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , ci    = newcombe
   , out   = eos_rd
 )
* Gives the risk difference of each flagged term against Placebo, within its class and term.;
%risk(
     data   = work.ae_flags
   , var    = flag
   , event  = "Y"
   , by     = trt01a
   , within = aebodsys aedecod
   , pairs  = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
            # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , ci     = newcombe
   , out    = ae_rd
 )
* Asks for the relative risk with measure=rr: the rows of STAT rr hold the ratio of the two risks.;
%risk(
     data    = adsl
   , var     = eosstt
   , event   = "DISCONTINUED"
   , by      = trt01a
   , order   = trt01an
   , measure = rr
   , out     = eos_rr
 )
* Stratifies by sex: the risk difference is the Mantel Haenszel estimate over the strata.;
%risk(
     data   = adsl
   , var    = eosstt
   , event  = "DISCONTINUED"
   , by     = trt01a
   , strata = sex
   , order  = trt01an
   , out    = eos_rd_mh
 )

macros.name: scatterplot
macros.purpose: Draws the values of two variables against each other as PNG and RTF files and returns the numbers drawn. Use %profileplot for the values of each subject over time. Typical uses are a shift plot of the baseline and post-baseline values, or two measures of a subject. Each group has its own colour and marker. With fit=linear, the least squares line of each group is drawn, and its slope, intercept and R-square are in out=. With fit=loess, the loess curve of SGPLOT is drawn; SGPLOT chooses its smoothing, and the curve is not in out=. With identity=yes, the line y = x is drawn. A record with a missing x, y, group or panel is not used. To draw the figure again without computing, give plot= the out= and par= the outpar= of an earlier call.
macros.proven: Its known answer: the points, and the slope, the intercept and the R-square of the line, worked out by hand; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-27 (the cases of the 9 figure macros: 103 of 103 the same)
macros.output: OUT: the variables of panel= and by=, KIND, X and Y. A row of KIND point is one value. With fit=linear, a row of KIND fit is one panel and group, with SLOPE, INTERCEPT, RSQUARE and N (X and Y missing). OUTPAR: one row per drawing parameter, in the order of the table: PARAMETER ($32), its name, and VALUE ($500), its value as drawn (a label in quotes). FILE: <file>.png and <file>.rtf.
macros.des: Two variables against each other by group (PROC REG, PROC SGPANEL)
macros.note: Draw again: plot= takes the out= of an earlier %scatterplot call, changed or not, and draws it as it is, with no statistic computed: its points, and the line of each row of KIND fit over the X of the points of its group (a loess curve is not in out= and is not drawn again). par= takes the outpar= of that call and gives the drawing parameters: columns, by, panel, identity, xlabel, ylabel, ref, file, width, height. These change the picture, not the numbers. The other parameters compute; with plot= the log has a NOTE for each one given, as it is not used. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=, and the row wins over the default of the table.

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: one record per point

parameters.name: plot
parameters.description: Draw again: the out= of an earlier %scatterplot call, changed or not. It is drawn as it is, and no statistic is computed. Give it instead of data=.

parameters.name: par
parameters.description: The drawing parameters of an earlier %scatterplot call: its outpar=. A drawing parameter given in the call wins over its row of par=.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.description: The data set of %columns: it gives the order of the groups and their colours. When not given, the groups come in the order of the data.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (anl01fl = 'Y')

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The variable of the x axis: one numeric variable (x = base)

parameters.name: y
