macros.name: stack
macros.purpose:
Stacks results one under another into one table, a block per result, in the order given. Call it before %columns, %ard and %layout, which read the stacked table. A result is the data set that a statistics macro writes (%describe, %freq, a test or a model): one row per number. Every result has the same variables, the result shape:
- the group variables, as in the data (TRT01A, AEDECOD, AVISIT ...); VERSUS: the group that a difference is made with
- GROUPS: the names of the group variables, in their order
- BLOCK: the label of the block
- STAT: the name of the statistic (n, pct, mean, pval ...)
- VALUE: the number
- TEXT: the number as printed
A block is the rows of one call in the table: the rows of one result, under its label. A DATA step of your own can write a result in the same shape. Each variable gets the longest length it has in the results, so that no text is cut.
macros.proven: The tables of a made-up study: every program ran with a clean log, and 570 of 570 numbers the same as those of a second program in R; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: all rows of the results in the result shape, with two more variables: RESULT, the name of the result that the row comes from, and ORD, the place of that result in the list (1, 2, ...). A result with no row keeps its number. A result named twice has the place of its first name. %layout lays out the blocks in the order of ORD.
macros.des: Put results one under another: the blocks of a table (a DATA step)

parameters.name: results
parameters.description: The results to stack: data set names separated by blanks, in the order of the blocks. Give them first, without a keyword (%stack(a b, out=t)), or as results= (%stack(results=a b, out=t)); a message names them results=.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the stacked table

macros.name: study
macros.purpose:
Starts a program: sets the study, the program and the output folder, opens the ADaM library, sets the options. Call it once, at the top of each program, before any other macro of the library. The ADaM library ADAM is read only. %ard names the numbers file after the program when its file= is not given. The macro also clears the TITLE and FOOTNOTE statements. The options, and why each is set:
- NODATE NONUMBER NOCENTER: no date and no page number at the top of a page, and the text starts at the left margin, as the outputs are laid out.
- LS=160: a line of a listing is 160 characters wide, the width of a landscape table.
- PS=32767: the longest page SAS has, so that SAS never breaks a part of a listing; %print starts each page itself (rows=).
- FORMDLIM=' ': a new page of the LISTING output is a blank line, not a form feed.
- MISSING=' ': a missing number prints as a blank, not as a period.
- VALIDVARNAME=UPCASE: the names of the variables a program makes are in upper case, as in the ADaM data sets.
- NOFMTERR: a format that is not found does not stop the program: the value prints with the default format, and the log has only a NOTE. The risk: a code prints in place of its label (F in place of Female); look for the NOTE "Format ... was not found" in the log.
To set an option back, write an OPTIONS statement after the call of %study: OPTIONS FMTERR stops the program again at a format that is not found, OPTIONS CENTER centers the output again.
macros.proven: Every program of a made-up study: each ran with a clean log, and 570 of 570 numbers the same as those of a second program in R; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: CODE: the global macro variables SPL_STUDY, SPL_PROGRAM (in lower case) and SPL_OUT; the library ADAM (read only); the options NODATE NONUMBER NOCENTER LS=160 PS=32767 MISSING=' ' VALIDVARNAME=upcase NOFMTERR FORMDLIM=' '; no TITLE and no FOOTNOTE.
macros.des: Start a program: the ADaM library, the output folder, the options

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The name of the study: a text without quotes, given first, without a keyword (%study(CDISCPILOT01, ...))

parameters.name: program
parameters.description: The name of this program, without quotes (program = t14_2_01). %ard names the numbers file after it when its file= is not given

parameters.name: adam
parameters.description: The folder of the ADaM data sets: a path without quotes. The macro opens it as the library ADAM, read only. SPL_ROOT is the folder of the library (it holds macros/): give adam= when the study is in a folder of its own.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The output folder: a path without quotes. The macros write into its folders tlf, listings, figures and ard. SPL_ROOT is the folder of the library (it holds macros/): give out= when the study is in a folder of its own.

macros.example:
* Starts the program of the examples: it sets SPL_STUDY, SPL_PROGRAM and SPL_OUT and opens ADAM.;
%study(
     CDISCPILOT01
   , program = examples
   , adam    = &spl_root./examples/adam
   , out     = &spl_root./examples/out
 )

macros.name: summarize
macros.purpose: Gives each subject the sum, mean, largest or smallest value of a variable over its records in another data set. Use %summarize_groups for one record per group instead of a new variable on each subject. A subject with no record gets a missing value. A sum of only missing values is missing. The rows of data= keep their order.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of a value summarized over the records of a subject (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: DATA: data=, changed in place: the variable new= on every row of a subject, with the sum, mean, maximum or minimum of value= over its records in from=. A subject with no record gets a missing value.
macros.des: The sum or mean of the records of each subject in another data set (PROC SUMMARY)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set to change in place, such as adsl

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The data set of the records, with USUBJID. When the value is not a variable yet, make it first in a DATA step.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The numeric variable of from= to summarize. To count records, give a 0/1 variable and stat=sum; for "some record meets it" use stat=max, for "every record meets it" stat=min.

parameters.name: stat
parameters.description: The statistic: sum, mean, max or min

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: The name of the new variable

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _summarize_*

macros.name: summarize_groups
macros.purpose: Returns one record per group with the sum, mean, largest or smallest value of each variable over the group. Use %summarize to add a summary of each subject's records to another data set. A missing value of a BY variable is a group of its own. A sum or a mean of only missing values is missing.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of a new parameter from the records of each subject (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: one record per group: the BY variables and the variables of vars=, each with its summary under its own name.
macros.des: One record per group with the sum, mean, largest or smallest value (PROC SUMMARY)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set. When a value is not a variable yet (a condition as 0 or 1), make it first in a DATA step.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one variable or several, separated by blanks (by = usubjid paramcd)

parameters.name: vars
parameters.description: The numeric variables to summarize, separated by blanks

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: One statistic for each variable of vars=, in the same order, separated by blanks: sum, mean, max or min (stats = sum max)

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the data set it writes

macros.example:
* Takes the largest AVAL and the smallest CHG of each subject and parameter: one record each.;
%summarize_groups(
     data  = advs
   , by    = usubjid paramcd
   , vars  = aval chg
   , stats = max min
   , out   = vs_extremes
 )

macros.name: table
macros.purpose: Makes a table from the stacked results in one call: %columns, %ard, %layout and %print, in that order. Use %table when the defaults of the four steps fit; call %columns, %ard, %layout and %print one by one to change a step between them. It passes them the same parameters as the separate calls and adds no logic of its own. The display data set is the data set %layout writes: one row per printed line, one column per printed column. The numbers file is the CSV file of %ard with every number of the table; the macro writes it only with file=, because it belongs to an output. The columns <data>_cols and the display data set out= stay in WORK. With setup=, a global macro variable also keeps the call of %print for out=: change out=, then print again with %print(&<setup>.). Without file=, the macro prints nothing: change out=, then call %print(&<setup>., file=...).
macros.proven: Its test cases: the same .lst and the same numbers file as the separate calls; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the display data set of %layout. DATA: <data>_cols, the columns of %columns. FILE: <file>.rtf and <file>.lst of %print, and the numbers file of %ard (only with file=). SETUP: with setup=, the global macro variable of that name, which holds the parameters of %print for out=.
macros.des: A table in one call: %columns, %ard, %layout and %print

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The results stacked by %stack: one data set in the result shape

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: The population for the N of each column: a data set with one row per subject (n= of %columns). When not given, the columns have no N.

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The column variable of the results: one variable, such as var = trt01a

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The numeric twin of var= in the data set of n=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns

parameters.name: total
parameters.description: yes: the results have the group Total, and it is the last column (total= of %columns). A text in quotes is another name for the Total.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The labels of the columns: pairs name="text", separated by blanks (label= of %print)

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: The number of rows a page holds: %print keeps the rows of one level on one page when they fit

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file <out>/ard/<last part of file>.csv. When not given, nothing is printed.

parameters.name: nodata
parameters.description: The text printed when the table has no row: a text in quotes

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: The name of a global macro variable that keeps the call of %print for out=. When not given, no macro variable is left.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the display data set. When not given, it is <data>_display.

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that %table calls

macros.example:
* Runs columns, ard, layout and print in one call: the same table as the long program.;
%table(
     data   = t14_2_1
   , n      = adsl
   , var    = trt01a
   , order  = trt01an
   , total  = yes
   , format = sex $sexf.
   , file   = &spl_out./tlf/t14_2_1_table
   , setup  = t14_2_1_table_print
 )

macros.name: table_ae
macros.purpose:
Makes a table of the subjects with adverse events by system organ class and preferred term in one call. Use it for any count of subjects by nested levels of records; to add a block that it does not make, start from its long program (show=). The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, the records, one %freq, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. A subject is counted once in each row, and the percent is of the subjects of the group. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:
- <name>_ae: the result, one row per number (the result shape, see %stack)
- <name>: the stacked results
- <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
- <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)
The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.).
macros.proven: Checked against its long program, written out by hand: the same display data set (PROC COMPARE), on a made-up study; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-13
macros.output: DATA: <name>_ae (the result), <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, <name>_pop (with adsl=) and <name>_rec (with adsl= or where=). FILE: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). SETUP: the global macro variable <name>_print. SHOW: the long program, in the log or in a file.
macros.des: An adverse event table in one call: subjects by the levels of var=

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records, with USUBJID

parameters.name: adsl
parameters.description: The subjects: a data set with one row per subject. It gives the population and the N of each column, and its variables are merged onto the records by USUBJID. When not given, the N of a column is the subjects of its records.

parameters.name: pop
parameters.description: The population: a condition on adsl= in parentheses, such as pop = (saffl = 'Y'). It is used only with adsl=.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The variables of the rows, nested in their order and separated by blanks, such as var = aebodsys aedecod

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: frequency: the rows of the last variable of var= in the order of their subjects, the most first (order=frequency of %freq). When not given, the rows are in the order of their values.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: A percent: keep only the rows whose percent of subjects reaches it in at least one group (threshold= of %freq), such as threshold = 5

parameters.name: total
parameters.description: yes: add the column Total, all groups together

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required.

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, each name with its pattern, separated by blanks (stats= of %freq), such as stats = n pct events

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used.

parameters.name: footnote
parameters.description: The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed.

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls

macros.example:
* Makes the table of the subjects with an event by class and term, each term by its subjects.;
%table_ae(
     data  = adam.adae
   , adsl  = adam.adsl
   , pop   = (saffl = 'Y')
   , where = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , var   = aebodsys aedecod
   , by    = trt01a
   , order = trt01an
   , sort  = frequency
   , label = "Treatment-emergent adverse events"
   , title = "Table 14.5.2 Treatment-emergent adverse events by SOC and PT"
   , file  = &spl_out./tlf/t14_5_2
 )
* Keeps the terms that reach 5 percent in a group, with the events and a Total column.;
%table_ae(
     data      = adae
   , adsl      = adsl
   , where     = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , var       = aedecod
   , by        = trt01a
   , order     = trt01an
   , sort      = frequency
   , threshold = 5
   , total     = yes
   , label     = "Subjects with an event, n (%) and events"
   , stats     = n pct events
   , title     = "Table 14.5.3 Common treatment-emergent adverse events"
   , file      = &spl_out./tlf/t14_5_3
 )

macros.name: table_model
macros.purpose:
Makes a table of a continuous endpoint in one call: descriptive statistics, and the LS means of a model. Use %table_visit for the statistics at every visit without a model; to add or change a block, start from its long program (show=). A block is the rows of one call in the table. The table has these blocks:
- one block per variable of describe=: its descriptive statistics on the records of the visit of at= (%describe)
- with method=ancova: the LS means and the differences of pairs of groups from an ANCOVA on the records of the visit of at= (%lsmeans), in a block with the label "ANCOVA, adjusted for" and the names of covars= in lower case, such as "ANCOVA, adjusted for base" (without covars=: "Analysis of variance")
- with method=mmrm: the same from a mixed model for repeated measures over all visits, at the visit of at= (%mmrm), in a block with the label "MMRM: " and the visit, such as "MMRM: Week 24"
With method=ancova, the records of the visit of at= must be one record per subject: give where= the parameter and the analysis flag, as %lsmeans uses the first record of a subject (with a NOTE when it leaves one out). The label of the model block is not changed by names=: change its row in <name>_display and print again, or start from the long program (show=). The table has no Total column. The long program is the program the macro writes and runs: the population, the records, one call per block, %stack and %table, the calls a person would write by hand. The macro computes nothing itself. These data sets stay in WORK, for a change and a second print:
- <name>_<variable> and <name>_ancova or <name>_mmrm: the results, one row per number (the result shape, see %stack)
- <name>: the stacked results
- <name>_cols: the columns (%columns)
- <name>_display: the display data set, one row per printed line (%layout)
The global macro variable <name>_print keeps the call of %print: change <name>_display, then print again with %print(&<name>_print.).
macros.proven: Checked against its long program, written out by hand: the same display data set (PROC COMPARE), on a made-up study; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-13
macros.output: DATA: <name>_<variable> (the descriptive results), <name>_ancova or <name>_mmrm (the result of the model), <name> (the stacked results), <name>_cols, <name>_display, <name>_at (with at=), <name>_pop (with adsl=) and <name>_rec (with adsl= or where=). FILE: <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file (only with file=). SETUP: the global macro variable <name>_print. SHOW: the long program, in the log or in a file. In the printed table, a comparison is in the column of the group, on the rows under "vs" and the group it is compared with: the LS mean of the column group minus the LS mean of the group on the row.
macros.des: A model table in one call: descriptive blocks, then ANCOVA or MMRM

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records, with USUBJID

parameters.name: adsl
parameters.description: The subjects: a data set with one row per subject. It gives the population and the N of each column, and its variables are merged onto the records by USUBJID. When not given, the N of a column is the subjects of its records.

parameters.name: pop
parameters.description: The population: a condition on adsl= in parentheses, such as pop = (saffl = 'Y'). It is used only with adsl=.

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The response: one numeric variable

parameters.name: covars
parameters.description: The covariates of the model, separated by blanks, such as covars = base

parameters.name: visit
parameters.description: The variable of the visit: one variable

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups of the columns: one character variable, such as by = trt01a

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: The visit of the table: a value of visit= in quotes, such as at = "Week 24". It selects the records of the descriptive blocks and of the ANCOVA, and the visit of the LS means of the MMRM. When not given, the ANCOVA uses all records.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The numeric twin of by=, such as order = trt01an: it gives the order of the columns and of the groups in the comparisons

parameters.name: describe
parameters.description: The variables with a descriptive block before the model, separated by blanks, such as describe = base aval chg

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: ancova (%lsmeans) or mmrm (%mmrm, which needs at=)

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: The fixed effects of the MMRM, separated by blanks. When not given: the covariates, the by= variable, the visit= variable and the interaction of the two (such as trt01p*avisit). This default has no interaction of a covariate with the visit, such as base*avisit: give model= to add one.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The covariance structure of the MMRM: TYPE= of the REPEATED statement, such as un, cs, ar(1) or toep (type= of %mmrm)

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: Other covariance structures of the MMRM to try in their order when one does not converge, separated by blanks, such as fallback = toep cs

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: The pairs of groups to compare, separated by #: each group in quotes, then the group it is compared with ("Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"). When not given, each later group is compared with each earlier one.

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: The labels of the blocks: pairs variable="text", separated by blanks, such as names = chg="Change from baseline". A block without a pair has the label of its variable, or its name.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: The labels of the categories: pairs of a variable and a format, as in a FORMAT statement (format = sex $sexf. race $racef.), as format= of %layout

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the table: the first part of the names of its data sets, such as name = t14_3_01. When not given, the last part of file= is used; without file=, name= is required.

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: yes: write the long program to the log. A file path, without quotes: write the long program to that file. In both cases the macro runs it.

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics of the model block, each name with its pattern. When not given: the LS means with their SE, the difference with its SE and limits, and the p-value.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: The titles of the table: one text in quotes per line (TITLE1, TITLE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the TITLE statements in force in the program are used.

parameters.name: footnote
parameters.description: The footnotes of the table: one text in quotes per line (FOOTNOTE1, FOOTNOTE2 ...). They hold for this table only. When not given, the FOOTNOTE statements in force in the program are used.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The output file without its extension: the macro writes <file>.rtf, <file>.lst and the numbers file. When not given, nothing is printed.

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets of the macros that the long program calls

macros.example:
* Makes the ANCOVA table at Week 12: three descriptive blocks, then the LS means and difference.;
%table_model(
     data     = advs
   , adsl     = adsl
   , where    = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND anl01fl = 'Y' AND avisitn < 99)
   , covars   = base
   , by       = trt01p
   , at       = "Week 12"
   , order    = trt01pn
   , describe = base aval chg
   , pairs    = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
   , title    = "Table 14.3.1 ANCOVA of the change of systolic blood pressure at Week 12"
   , file     = &spl_out./tlf/t14_3_1
 )
* Uses method=mmrm with the model of the mmrm example: the same differences at Week 24.;
%table_model(
     data     = advs
   , adsl     = adsl
   , where    = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND anl01fl = 'Y' AND avisitn IN (4 8 12 16 24))
   , covars   = base
   , visit    = avisit
   , by       = trt01p
   , at       = "Week 24"
   , order    = trt01pn
   , method   = mmrm
   , model    = base trt01p avisit trt01p*avisit base*avisit
   , type     = un
   , fallback = toep
   , title    = "Table 14.3.3 MMRM of the change of systolic blood pressure at Week 24"
   , file     = &spl_out./tlf/t14_3_3
 )

macros.name: table_response
macros.purpose:
Makes a response table in one call: the responders in each group, and the comparisons of pairs of groups. Use %table_ae to count the subjects by levels of events; to add or change a block, start from its long program (show=). A block is the rows of one call in the table. The table has these blocks:

- with time=: the percent without an event at that time and its limits (%km)

parameters.name: show

parameters.name: stats

parameters.name: title

parameters.name: footnote

parameters.name: file

macros.example:

%table_visit(

macros.name: termflags
macros.purpose: Returns one record per subject and term, with a flag that says whether the subject has the term. Use it before %risk to compare the groups on the subjects with a term; %freq counts the subjects but gives no flag per subject. The macro computes no statistic. A term is each combination of the values of terms= in the records. FLAG is "Y" when the subject has a record of the term and "N" when not. The subjects are those of denom=: a subject with a record who is not in denom= is left out. Then %risk compares the groups on FLAG within each term (within= the variables of terms=), with the subjects of each group as the denominator.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer: the risk difference of each term of an adverse event table (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: one record per subject of denom= and term: USUBJID, the variable of by=, the variables of terms= and FLAG ("Y" or "N"), sorted by the variables of terms= and USUBJID.
macros.des: The flag Y or N of each term for every subject of the population (PROC SORT, MERGE)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records of the events, with USUBJID

parameters.name: denom
parameters.description: The subjects of the groups: a data set with one row per subject (the population), with USUBJID and the variable of by=

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y')

parameters.name: terms
parameters.description: The variables of a row: one or several, separated by blanks, nested in their order (terms = aebodsys aedecod: a term within its class). When not given, one row of all the records, such as "any event" of an overview table.

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one variable of denom=

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: A percent (threshold = 5): keep only the terms with this percent of the subjects or more in at least one group. The macro compares the percent itself, not its rounded text. It needs terms=.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _termflags_*

macros.example:
* Flags each subject for each term that reaches 5 percent: FLAG is Y with the term, N without.;
%termflags(
     data      = adae
   , denom     = adsl
   , where     = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , terms     = aebodsys aedecod
   , by        = trt01a
   , threshold = 5
   , out       = ae_flags
 )

macros.name: tte
macros.purpose:
Returns one time-to-event parameter: for each subject the date of the first event, or else of the latest censoring. It writes the records of an ADTTE parameter; %km, %logrank and %cox then analyse them. The rule:
- An event is a record of events= that meets event= and has a date. The first event of a subject is taken; priority= orders the events of one date.
- When a subject has no event, the latest censoring is taken: the latest date of censors= (or of subjects=); on one date, the last record.
- AVAL is ADT - START + 1, in days.
Without end=, every date counts, and a date before START becomes START (as admiral does). A subject with no event and no censoring date gets no record, and the log has a NOTE with the number of such subjects. With end=, the at-risk period runs from START to END: only the events and censorings in it count, and a subject with neither is censored at END. An event on the start day counts unless time= and start_time= are both there and the event time is before the start time.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of the time to an event, also within a period (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: one record per subject with an event, a censoring or (with end=) a period, in the order of subjects=: the variables of subjects=, PARAMCD, ADT, CNSR, AVAL, ATM (with time=), EVNTDESC, SRCDOM, SRCVAR, SRCSEQ, ADTF and ATMF (when their parameters are given) and the variables of keep=. With end=, a subject with no START or no END gets no record and a WARNING that names it; a subject whose START is after its END gets no record. Two records of a subject in subjects= give an ERROR line. Without end=, a subject with no event and no censoring date gets no record, and a NOTE gives their number.
macros.des: One time-to-event parameter: the first event, else the latest censoring (PROC SORT)

parameters.name: subjects
parameters.description: The data set of the subjects, one record per subject (USUBJID), with the start (and the end) of the period. The result keeps its variables, so it must not have ADT, CNSR, AVAL or the other variables the macro makes.

parameters.name: events
parameters.description: The data set of the records the events come from, such as adae

parameters.name: censors
parameters.description: The data set of the records of the censorings, with censor_date=. When not given, the censorings come from subjects=.

parameters.name: event
parameters.description: The records of events= that are events: a condition, such as event = trtemfl = 'Y'. When not given, every record with a date is an event.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The date of an event: a numeric date variable of events=. A record with a missing date is no event.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: The time of an event: a numeric variable of events=, in seconds since midnight. It decides an event on the start day, and needs end=.

parameters.name: priority
parameters.description: The variables of events= that order the events of one date, separated by blanks; a missing value sorts last. When not given, the events of one date keep the order of the data.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The start of the period and the origin of AVAL: a date variable of subjects=

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: The time of the start: a numeric variable of subjects=, in seconds since midnight. On the start day an event counts unless its time is before this time. It needs end=.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The end of the at-risk period: a date variable of subjects=. When not given, there is no period and every date counts.

parameters.name: censor_date
parameters.description: The date of a censoring: a date variable of censors= (or of subjects=)

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: The variable of events= that gives SRCSEQ of an event, such as aeseq. When not given, SRCSEQ is missing.

parameters.name: adtf
parameters.description: The variable of events= that gives ADTF, the imputation flag of the date of an event

parameters.name: atmf
parameters.description: The variable of events= that gives ATMF, the imputation flag of the time of an event

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Other variables of the record taken, separated by blanks: they must be in events= and in censors= both

parameters.name: censor_cnsr
parameters.description: CNSR of a censoring: a number, or a numeric variable of censors=

parameters.name: end_cnsr
parameters.description: CNSR of a subject censored at the end of the period: a number

parameters.name: censor_desc
parameters.description: EVNTDESC of a censoring: a text in quotes, or a variable of censors= (or of subjects=)

parameters.name: censor_source
parameters.description: SRCDOM of a censoring from subjects= and of a censoring at the end of the period: a text in quotes, such as "ADSL". SRCVAR is then the name of censor_date= (or of end=).

parameters.name: end_desc
parameters.description: EVNTDESC of a subject censored at the end of the period: a text in quotes

parameters.name: event_desc
parameters.description: EVNTDESC of an event: a text in quotes, or a variable of events=, such as aedecod

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: SRCDOM of an event: a text in quotes, such as "ADAE". SRCVAR is then the name of date=.

parameters.name: paramcd
parameters.description: PARAMCD of the parameter: a text in quotes, such as "TTDE"

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the data set it writes

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _tte_*

macros.example:
* Derives the time to the first skin event from the first dose: CNSR 0 is an event, 1 a censoring.;
%tte(
     subjects      = adsl
   , events        = adae
   , event         = trtemfl = 'Y' AND aebodsys = 'SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE DISORDERS'
   , date          = astdt
   , start         = trtsdt
   , censor_date   = trtedt
   , seq           = aeseq
   , censor_desc   = "End of treatment"
   , censor_source = "ADSL"
   , event_desc    = aedecod
   , source        = "ADAE"
   , paramcd       = "TTDE"
   , out           = adttde
 )

macros.name: ttest
macros.purpose:
Returns the difference of the means of each pair of groups, with its confidence limits and the t-test p-value. Use %wilcoxon when the values are not normal, %anova for one test of all the groups, and %lsmeans for a model with covariates. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The test is the two-sample t-test of PROC TTEST, run BY each pair, the group first. The statistics:
- diff: the mean of the group minus the mean of the group it is compared with
- diff_se: the standard error of diff
- lcl, ucl: the confidence limits of diff
- pval: the two-sided p-value, of Student's test with the pooled variance (variances=equal) or of Welch's test with Satterthwaite's degrees of freedom (variances=unequal)
The macro uses one record per subject: when a subject has several records, the first one.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per pair and statistic: the variable of by= (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), GROUPS (by= and VERSUS), BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies, the result has no row.
macros.des: The two-sample t-test of each pair of groups (PROC TTEST)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The variable to compare: one numeric variable

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one character variable (trt01a, not trt01an)

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: Which groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (else of the values). Or the pairs, separated by #: in each pair the group first, then the group it is compared with, each value in quotes (pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low")

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01an)

parameters.name: variances
parameters.description: equal (Student's test, the Pooled row of PROC TTEST) or unequal (Welch's test, the Satterthwaite row)

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1 (level = 0.90)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are diff, diff_se, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _ttest_*

macros.example:
* Compares each pair of groups with the pooled t test: the difference, its SE, limits and p value.;
%ttest(
     data  = advs
   , where = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12' AND anl01fl = 'Y')
   , var   = chg
   , by    = trt01p
   , order = trt01pn
   , out   = sbp_t
 )
* Uses the Welch test of unequal variances on two pairs: the SE, limits and p value change.;
%ttest(
     data      = advs
   , where     = (paramcd = 'SYSBP' AND avisit = 'Week 12' AND anl01fl = 'Y')
   , var       = chg
   , by        = trt01p
   , pairs     = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
               # "Xanomeline Low Dose"  "Placebo"
   , variances = unequal
   , out       = sbp_welch
 )

macros.name: visits
macros.purpose: Gives each record its analysis visit, AVISIT and AVISITN, from the value of its variable VISIT. Use %windows when the analysis visit comes from the study day of the record. The value of VISIT must match exactly, in upper and lower case. A record whose visit is not in visits= gets missing values only when data= does not have AVISIT and AVISITN yet. When data= has them already (from an earlier step), a record whose visit is not in visits= keeps its old AVISIT and AVISITN: drop them before the call when such a record must have none.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of the analysis visit of each collected visit (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: DATA: data=, changed in place: AVISIT and AVISITN on each record whose visit is in visits=, missing on the others.
macros.des: Give each record its analysis visit by its visit (a DATA step)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set to change in place, with the variable VISIT, such as adlb

parameters.name: visits
parameters.description: The visits, separated by #. Each visit is "VISIT" AVISITN "AVISIT": the value of VISIT in quotes, then the analysis visit as a number and as a text (# "WEEK 2" 2 "Week 2").

macros.name: wilcoxon
macros.purpose:
Returns the p-value of the Wilcoxon rank-sum test of each pair of groups, with the Hodges-Lehmann shift and its limits. Use %ttest when the values are normal and the difference of the means is wanted. The macro writes a result: a data set with one row per number (the result shape, see %stack). The test runs in PROC NPAR1WAY, BY each pair, the group first. The statistics:
- pval: the two-sided p-value of the normal approximation, with the continuity correction when correction=yes (CORRECT=)
- estimate: the Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the shift, the group minus the group it is compared with (HL)
- lcl, ucl: the asymptotic (Moses) confidence limits of the shift
The macro uses one record per subject: when a subject has several records, the first one.
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer (on a small data set, the numbers worked out independently in R); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the result shape (see %stack), one row per pair and statistic: the variable of by= (the group), VERSUS (the group it is compared with), GROUPS (by= and VERSUS), BLOCK, STAT, VALUE and TEXT. When no record qualifies, the result has no row.
macros.des: The Wilcoxon rank-sum test and Hodges-Lehmann shift of pairs (PROC NPAR1WAY)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: one record per subject, with USUBJID

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (avisit = 'Week 24')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The variable to compare: one numeric variable

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The groups: one character variable (trt01a, not trt01an)

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: Which groups to compare. all: each later group against each earlier one, in the order of order= (else of the values). Or the pairs, separated by #: in each pair the group first, then the group it is compared with, each value in quotes (pairs = "Drug" "Placebo" # "High" "Low")

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order of the groups: one numeric variable with one value per group (order = trt01an)

parameters.name: correction
parameters.description: yes: the continuity correction of the normal approximation; no: none

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: The confidence level: a number between 0 and 1 (level = 0.90)

parameters.name: stats
parameters.description: The statistics, in the order of the rows: each name with its pattern of the printed number, separated by blanks. The names are estimate, lcl, ucl and pval. A name without a pattern takes its default pattern: see the table of default patterns (How a number is kept and printed).

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The label of the block in the table: a text in quotes. A block is the rows of one call in the table.

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the result data set

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _wilcoxon_*

macros.example:
* Compares each pair with the Wilcoxon rank sum test and the Hodges Lehmann estimate.;
%wilcoxon(
     data  = advs
   , where = (paramcd = 'DIABP' AND avisit = 'Week 12' AND anl01fl = 'Y')
   , var   = chg
   , by    = trt01p
   , order = trt01pn
   , out   = dbp_w
 )
* Leaves out the continuity correction for one pair: only the p value changes.;
%wilcoxon(
     data       = advs
   , where      = (paramcd = 'DIABP' AND avisit = 'Week 12' AND anl01fl = 'Y')
   , var        = chg
   , by         = trt01p
   , pairs      = "Xanomeline High Dose" "Placebo"
   , correction = no
   , out        = dbp_w_nocc
 )

macros.name: windows
macros.purpose:
Puts each record into its analysis window by its study day, and gives it AVISIT, AVISITN and the window variables. Use %visits when the analysis visit comes from the visit name of the record, not from its study day. The macro writes these variables:
- AVISIT and AVISITN: the analysis visit of the window
- AWLO, AWHI and AWTARGET: the first day, the last day and the target day of the window
- AWRANGE: the window as a text; AWU: DAYS
- AWTDIFF: the distance of the study day to the target day
A record takes the first window, in the order of windows=, that holds its day. A record with no window, or a missing day, gets missing values only when data= does not have these variables yet. When data= has them already (an AVISIT from an earlier step), a record in no window keeps its old AVISIT, AVISITN and window values: drop them before the call when such a record must have none.
macros.proven: Checked on its test cases of the analysis visit of each study day (small made-up records): every value the same as that of the expected records; ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: DATA: data=, changed in place: AVISIT, AVISITN, AWLO, AWHI, AWTARGET, AWRANGE, AWU and AWTDIFF on each record in a window, missing on a record in no window.
macros.des: Put each record in its analysis window by its study day (a DATA step)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The data set to change in place, such as advs

parameters.name: windows
parameters.description: The windows in the order of AVISITN, separated by #. Each window is AVISITN "AVISIT" AWLO AWHI AWTARGET "AWRANGE"; a period for AWLO or AWHI is a limit that is open (# 4 "Week 4" 2 42 28 "2-42").

parameters.name: day
parameters.description: The numeric variable of the study day

macros.name: worst
macros.purpose: Keeps the records of each subject at its worst level, such as the highest severity or toxicity grade. Use it before %freq, so that %freq counts each subject once in each row, at its worst level; the macro computes no statistic. The worst level is the value of var= that comes last in levels= (levels= goes from the least to the most severe). The macro looks for it for each subject in each row of by=, or in all the records of the subject when by= is not given. A record whose value is not in levels=, such as a missing grade, is never the worst and is left out. When a subject has several records at its worst level, all of them stay.
macros.procedure: PROC SORT, a DATA step (BY, FIRST.)
macros.proven: Checked against its known answer: the worst records counted by hand (a second program in R gives the same); ran on SAS 9.4 M9, 2026-11-12
macros.output: OUT: the records of data= at the worst level of each subject and row, with all the variables of data=, sorted by USUBJID and the variables of by=.
macros.des: The records of each subject at its worst level (PROC SORT, a DATA step)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: The input data set: the records, with USUBJID

parameters.name: where
parameters.description: The records to use: a condition in parentheses, such as where = (trtemfl = 'Y')

parameters.name: var
parameters.description: The graded variable: one variable, character or numeric (var = aesev)

parameters.name: by
parameters.description: The variables of a row: one or several, separated by blanks (by = aebodsys aedecod). The macro keeps the worst records of each subject in each row. When not given, the worst of all the records of the subject.

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: The values of var= from the least to the most severe, separated by blanks: texts in quotes, numbers without (levels = 'MILD' 'MODERATE' 'SEVERE')

parameters.name: out
parameters.description: The name of the data set of the records kept

parameters.name: debug
parameters.description: yes: keep the work data sets _worst_*

macros.example:
* Keeps the records of each subject and term at the worst severity, the last value of levels=.;
%worst(
     data   = adae
   , where  = (trtemfl = 'Y')
   , var    = aesev
   , by     = aebodsys aedecod
   , levels = 'MILD' 'MODERATE' 'SEVERE'
   , out    = ae_worst
 )
